title: Cessna Citation CJ4 (Asobo)
notice: The engine start (and the lights, parking brake, flaps and the other switches it uses) was run on a real CJ4: a full start was done through the app and its checks read back from the sim. The other topics are written from the CJ4 Operator's Guide, the Working Title guide and the aircraft's own files (every step names its source); their ticks and answers, and the FMS key sequences, have not been run on the aircraft yet, so tick by hand if one never appears. MSFS 2024: the same guide; where MSFS 2024 renamed a control (battery, avionics, landing lights) the step shows both, and the avionics ticks read whichever the sim reports. The 2024 CJ4 was checked with its engines running (2026-11-06), not through a full start.
sources: CJ4_Checklist.xml shipped with the aircraft (Official/Steam/asobo-aircraft-cj4/SimObjects/Airplanes/Asobo_CJ4/Checklist), the sim's own interactive checklist
State variables read from a running CJ4 (MSFS 11.0.282174.999)

MSFS Cessna Citation CJ4 Model 525C Operator's Guide (v1), published by Microsoft Flight Simulator: https://flightsimulator.azureedge.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/Cessna-Citation-CJ4-User-Guide-v1.pdf

Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF, simulation use only, not official): https://digitalthemepark.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/checklist-cj4_workingtitle.pdf

es_ground.title: Where is the aircraft?
es_ground.text: Is the aircraft on the ground?
es_ground.help: The engines are started on the ground. The answer is filled in from the simulator when it can tell.

choices.label: Yes, it is on the ground

es_air.title: Not on the ground
es_air.text: This guide covers the engine start on the ground, which is the only start the sim's own CJ4 checklist describes. Land and park first, then come back.
es_air.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: only the PREFLIGHT_GATE step has pages: before starting, starting, after starting

es_state.title: Engines
es_state.help: Both engines running means the start is done; the guide then goes straight to the checks after the start.

auto.code: (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:2, Bool) +

es_which.title: Which engine is running?
es_which.help: The sim's checklist starts the right engine first, then repeats the procedure for the left one.

steps.text: Set the parking brake.
steps.where: The sim's own checklist looks at its camera Instrument04 for this step.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: Parking_Brake_Set

steps.text: Put both power levers at IDLE.
steps.where: The sim's own checklist looks at its camera Instrument05 for this step.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: POWER_LEVERS_IDLE_2ENGINES

check.code: (A:GENERAL ENG THROTTLE LEVER POSITION:1, percent) (A:GENERAL ENG THROTTLE LEVER POSITION:2, percent) +

steps.text: Turn both generator switches ON.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: GENERATOR_MAIN_2 (subject: generator switches, expectation: ON)

check.code: (A:GENERAL ENG MASTER ALTERNATOR:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG MASTER ALTERNATOR:2, Bool) +

steps.text: Turn the battery switch ON.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: Battery_Switch_On_CJ4

steps.text: Set the avionics master switch to DISPATCH.
steps.why: The sim's clue for this step is "avionics master switch: dispatch". The switch has three positions; the checklist sets position 2 now and position 0 (ON) after the engines are started.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: Avionics_Bus_Switch_On, clue AVIONICS_MASTER_SWITCH_DISPATCH, value 2 of B:ELECTRICAL_Avionics_Bus_1

steps.text: Turn the right engine starter ON.
steps.where: The sim's own checklist looks at its camera Instrument06 for this step.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: RIGHT_ENGINE_STARTER_ON

steps.text: When N2 reaches 20 %, press the right RUN button.
steps.where: The sim's own checklist looks at its camera Instrument05 for this step.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: RIGHT_ENG_RUN_BUTTON_RUN_WHEN_N2_20

steps.text: Watch ITT and N1 on the MFD during the start.
steps.where: The sim's own checklist looks at its camera Instrument01 for this step. They are shown on the MFD.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: ITT_AND_N1_MONITOR (instruments WT21_MFD_1 N1 and ITT)

es_left.title: Start the left engine
es_left.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: LEFT_ENGINE_START_REPEAT_PROCEDURE_JET: repeat the procedure for the left engine

steps.text: Turn the left engine starter ON.
steps.where: The sim's own checklist looks at its camera Instrument06 for this step.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: LEFT_ENGINE_START_REPEAT_PROCEDURE_JET, instrument ENGINE_Switch_Starter1

steps.text: When N2 reaches 20 %, press the left RUN button.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: LEFT_ENGINE_START_REPEAT_PROCEDURE_JET (repeat the procedure)

steps.text: Watch ITT and N1 on the MFD during the start.
steps.where: The sim's own checklist looks at its camera Instrument01 for this step. They are shown on the MFD.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: ITT_AND_N1_MONITOR (instruments WT21_MFD_1 N1 and ITT)

steps.text: Set the avionics master switch to ON.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: Avionics_Bus_Switch_On, value 0 of B:ELECTRICAL_Avionics_Bus_1 after the start

steps.text: Turn on the beacon, navigation, strobe and taxi lights.
steps.where: The sim's own checklist looks at its camera Instrument03 for this step.
steps.why: The sim's checklist considers this step done when these four lights are on.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: LIGHTS_AS_REQUIRED_CUSTOM

check.code: (A:LIGHT BEACON, Bool) (A:LIGHT NAV, Bool) + (A:LIGHT STROBE, Bool) + (A:LIGHT TAXI, Bool) +

steps.text: Release the parking brake.
steps.where: The sim's own checklist looks at its camera Instrument04 for this step.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: Parking_Brake_Release

es_done.title: Engines started
es_done.text: Both engines are running, the avionics master is ON and the parking brake is released: this is the end of the sim's start-up checklist.

pu_ground.title: Where is the aircraft?
pu_ground.text: Is the aircraft on the ground?
pu_ground.help: The power-up is a ground procedure. The answer is filled in from the simulator when it can tell.

choices.label: Yes, it is on the ground

pu_air.title: Not on the ground
pu_air.text: The power-up procedure is for the ground. The sources only describe the cockpit preparation before the engine start, so there is nothing to follow in the air. If you need to restart an engine in flight, this guide has no sourced procedure.
pu_air.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: only the PREFLIGHT_GATE step has pages (before starting, starting, after starting); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 3 Engine start

pu_batt_q.title: Battery
pu_batt_q.help: If the cockpit already has power you can skip the battery step: the next steps tick themselves when they are already done.

choices.label: No, the cockpit is cold and dark

pu_batt.title: Battery
pu_batt.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: Battery_Switch_On_CJ4; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE START

steps.text: Turn the battery switch ON.
steps.why: The battery master switch supplies the main electrical power to the aircraft (guide, electrical panel). In the catalog, setting the switch to 0 turns the battery ON and 1 turns it OFF.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: Battery_Switch_On_CJ4 (also Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE START item 1)

pu_gen.title: Generators, avionics, emergency lights
pu_gen.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: BEFORE STARTING ENGINE page; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE START; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 Electrical panel

steps.text: Turn both generator switches ON.
steps.why: The generators feed the main electrical bus once the engines run. The guide says both switches should be ON as per the cockpit preparation checklist.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: GENERATOR_MAIN_2 (subject: generator switches, expectation: ON); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 L/R GEN

check.code: (A:GENERAL ENG MASTER ALTERNATOR:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG MASTER ALTERNATOR:2, Bool) +

steps.text: Put the emergency lights switch on ARMED.
steps.why: If it is not armed the crew alerting system shows EMER LIGHTS NOT ARMED. Emergency lighting itself is not modelled in the sim, but the alert reads the switch (guide).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE START item 2; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 EMER LIGHTS

steps.text: Turn the standby flight display switch ON.
steps.why: The standby flight display is the small backup instrument. No catalog control exists for this switch.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE START item 3; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 STBY FLT DISPLAY

steps.text: Set the avionics master switch to DISPATCH.
steps.why: In DISPATCH only the left MFD and the left FMS are powered, so you can work on the flight plan before the engines run (guide). The switch has three positions (catalog: 1 = OFF, 0 = ON, 2 = DISPATCH); the sim's checklist uses DISPATCH now and ON after the engine start.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: Avionics_Bus_Switch_On, clue AVIONICS_MASTER_SWITCH_DISPATCH; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE START item 4

steps.text: Set the parking brake.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: Parking_Brake_Set; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE START item 5

pu_gpu_q.title: Ground power
pu_gpu_q.text: Is a ground power unit available at your parking spot?
pu_gpu_q.help: Ground power only exists at parking spots that have it. The USER SETTINGS page of the FMS shows AVAIL or NOT AVAIL. You do not need it to start the engines.

choices.label: Yes, I want to use it
No, or I will not use it

pu_gpu.title: Ground power
pu_gpu.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class UserSettingsPage and IndexPage; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 MOD SET (GROUND POWER UNIT)

steps.text: Press the IDX key on the pilot's CDU.
steps.why: The CDU is the keypad and screen of the FMS. IDX opens the INDEX page.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class IndexPage (page 1/2)

steps.text: Press the NEXT page key to reach page 2 of the INDEX.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class IndexPage (page 2/2)

steps.text: Press LSK R6 (SETTINGS>).
steps.why: LSK means line select key: the six keys on each side of the screen. R6 is the lowest key on the right.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class IndexPage: userSetLink on line 6 right

steps.text: Press LSK L1 (GROUND POWER) to switch it ON.
steps.why: The guide: ground power is applied to the aircraft where available, at a designated parking spot that has a ground power unit. If the label says NOT AVAIL the FMS puts the switch back to OFF.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class UserSettingsPage: groundPowerSwitch (OFF/ON) and AVAIL / NOT AVAIL label

pu_done.title: Cockpit powered
pu_done.text: Battery, generators, emergency lights, avionics (DISPATCH) and parking brake are set. Next, open the topic Start the engines, then Set up the flight plan in the FMS.

fp_ground.title: Where is the aircraft?
fp_ground.text: Is the aircraft on the ground?
fp_ground.help: The origin airport can only be set on the ground. The answer is filled in from the simulator when it can tell.

fp_air.title: In the air
fp_air.text: The origin cannot be changed in flight (the FMS answers NOT ON GROUND). The destination, the arrival and the approach can still be changed at any time: open the topic Change the flight plan in flight.
fp_air.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN (ORIGIN: cannot be modified once airborne; DEST: can be modified at any time); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FplnPageController.setOrigin (throws NOT ON GROUND)

fp_pos.title: Set the position
fp_pos.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 STATUS and POS INIT; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, classes IndexPage, PosInitPage, FmsPos

steps.text: Press the IDX key on the pilot's CDU.
steps.why: The CDU is the keypad and screen of the FMS. These steps use the pilot's (left) CDU. IDX opens the INDEX page.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class IndexPage

steps.text: Press LSK L3 (<POS INIT).
steps.why: LSK means line select key: the six keys on each side of the screen. L3 is the third one down on the left.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class IndexPage: posInitLink on line 3 left

steps.text: Press LSK R4 to copy the GPS position into SET POS.
steps.why: Until the position is set the CDU shows the message INITIALIZE POSITION. The line above the key reads SET POS TO GNSS and changes to COMPLETE once it is done. If it already says COMPLETE, nothing is left to do: the sim sets the position by itself when the flight starts with the battery on.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 POS INIT (press LSK 4R); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class PosInitPage.onHandleSelectKey (right key, line 4)

fp_src.title: Route source
fp_src.text: Where does your route come from?
fp_src.help: SimBrief import needs an internet connection and your SimBrief pilot ID or user name. It fills the origin, destination, route, alternate, flight number and cruise altitude.

choices.label: I made a flight plan on the world map before the flight
I will type it in the FMS

fp_world.title: Plan from the world map
fp_world.text: When the flight starts, the FMS loads the flight plan of the world map (origin, destination, departure and arrival procedures, approach and enroute waypoints) and, if the battery is ON at that moment, activates it by itself. Check the FPLN and LEGS pages. If the plan is empty or wrong, load it from SimBrief or type it in the FMS. Every EXEC saves the FMS plan back to the simulator's own flight plan.
fp_world.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, classes FlightPlanAsoboSync (loadFromGame, setDeparture, setDestination, SaveToGame) and WT21_FMC_Instrument.onFlightStart; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 1 Flight plan synchronization

fp_sb.title: Load the route from SimBrief
fp_sb.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, classes UserSettingsPage, RouteMenuPage, FmcFplnRequestSystem; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 1 SimBrief

steps.text: Press IDX.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class IndexPage (SETTINGS> is on page 2, line 6 right)

steps.text: Press the NEXT page key.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class IndexPage (SETTINGS> is on page 2, line 6 right)

steps.text: Press LSK R6 (SETTINGS>).
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class IndexPage (SETTINGS> is on page 2, line 6 right)

steps.text: Type your SimBrief pilot ID (digits) or user name, then press LSK L3 (SIMBRIEF ID).
steps.why: The pilot ID is a 5 or 6 digit number shown in the SimBrief dispatch options (guide). It is stored, so you only do this once. INVALID SB USER means the name was not found.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class UserSettingsPage.simbriefUsernameField (accepts digits or a user name)

steps.text: Press IDX.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class IndexPage (ROUTE MENU> on page 1, line 6 right)

steps.text: Press LSK R6 (ROUTE MENU>).
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class IndexPage (ROUTE MENU> on page 1, line 6 right)

steps.text: Press LSK L3 (<FPLN RECALL).
steps.why: The FMS fetches your SimBrief flight plan and shows the FPLN page. DL FPLN LOADED means it worked, DL FPLN FAILED means it did not (check the ID and the internet connection).
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class RouteMenuPage: fplnRecallField; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 1 SIMBRIEF

steps.text: Press EXEC to make the new plan active.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 1 SIMBRIEF (prompted to hit EXEC to finalize)

fp_route.title: Origin and destination
fp_route.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN (ACT FPLN); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, classes FplnPage, FplnPageController

steps.text: Press the FPLN key.
steps.why: The ACT FPLN page is where you start building the flight plan.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN

steps.text: Type the departure airport code on the CDU keyboard, for example KCRQ.
steps.why: What you type appears on the last line of the screen, the scratchpad. A line select key then moves it into the field next to the key. CLR deletes the last character.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN (ORIGIN: 3 or 4 letter ICAO code)

steps.text: Press LSK L1 (ORIGIN).
steps.why: If the CDU says NOT IN DATABASE (this sim says FACILITY NOT FOUND) for a code that is valid, press the key again or clear the message and retry (guide note).
steps.warn: Setting a new origin clears the current flight plan.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FplnPageController.setOrigin

steps.text: Type the destination airport code and press LSK R1 (DEST).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN (DEST: can be modified at any time)

steps.text: If the page title shows MOD, press EXEC.
steps.why: MOD means the change is not active yet. EXEC makes it active.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEPART (MOD stays until EXEC is pressed); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FplnPageController.modHeaderString

fp_dep.title: Departure runway and SID
fp_dep.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEP ARR, DEP/ARR INDEX, DEPART; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class DepArrPage

steps.text: Press the DEP ARR key.
steps.why: On the ground it opens the DEP/ARR INDEX or the DEPART page of your origin.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEP ARR

steps.text: If the DEP/ARR INDEX is shown, press LSK L1 (<DEP).
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class DepArrPage.getIndexTemplate and onHandleSelectKey (left key, line 1)

steps.text: Choose the departure runway on the right of the page.
steps.why: Not every runway fits every SID. Pick the SID first to see its runways, or pick the runway first to see its SIDs (guide note). NEXT and PREV show more pages.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEPART (RUNWAYS selection) and TAKEOFF (RWY ID: departure runway selected from the DEP page, required for the speeds)

steps.text: If ATC gave you a SID, choose it on the left, then its transition if the list shows one.
steps.why: SID means standard instrument departure. A SID is not required. The chosen items turn green; press a green item again to remove it.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEPART

steps.text: Press EXEC.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEPART (MOD in the top left corner until EXEC has been pressed)

fp_en_q.title: Route
fp_en_q.text: Does your route use airways or named waypoints?

fp_enroute.title: Enroute airways and waypoints
fp_enroute.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN (VIA / TO, page 2 and later); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FplnPageController.takeAirwayEntry and takeLegEntry

steps.text: Press the FPLN key.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN (VIA will not take user input on page 1: airways must be entered on page 2 or higher)

steps.text: Press the NEXT page key.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN (VIA will not take user input on page 1: airways must be entered on page 2 or higher)

steps.text: To fly an airway, type its name (for example J1) and press the left key of a free VIA row.
steps.why: The airway must pass through the waypoint of the row above, otherwise the CDU says AIRWAY NOT FOUND.
steps.warn: Enter the airways before any STAR or approach: a STAR or approach already in the plan can prevent airway entries (guide).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN (enter the airway first with the left LSKs); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FplnPageController.takeAirwayEntry

steps.text: Type the waypoint where you leave the airway and press the right key (TO) of the same row.
steps.why: The exit must be on that airway (INVALID AIRWAY EXIT otherwise) and on the same row as the airway (INVALID LINE SELECTED otherwise).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN (connect it to an exit using the opposite right LSK); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FplnPageController.takeLegEntry

steps.text: To fly direct to a waypoint, type its name and press the right key (TO) of a free row.
steps.why: Use a VOR, NDB, intersection or airport. Custom waypoints are not accepted here: enter them on the LEGS page.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN (waypoints entered without an airway always show as DIRECT)

steps.text: Press EXEC.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN

fp_legs.title: Check the legs
fp_legs.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 LEGS and CONSTRAINTS; MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 VNAV operation

steps.text: Press the LEGS key.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 LEGS (after entering the flight plan, check the LEGS page)

steps.text: Check every waypoint and its speed and altitude restriction on the right.
steps.why: Restrictions from the SID, STAR and approach are loaded automatically. The CJ4 has no autothrottle, so speed restrictions are advice only. Altitude restrictions are used by VNAV. The right column does not need your cruise altitude (guide).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 LEGS CONSTRAINTS

steps.text: To add a restriction, type it and press the right key next to the waypoint. Examples: 250/18000, 18000B, 9000A.
steps.why: 250/18000 is 250 kt at 18,000 ft, 18000B is at or below 18,000 ft, 9000A is at or above 9,000 ft. A number below 500 is read as a speed: to enter an altitude below 500 type a / first, for example /400.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 CONSTRAINTS (valid formats)

steps.text: Look for a gap marked with boxes (a discontinuity). If there is one, press CLR then the left key next to it.
steps.why: A gap is a break in the route, for example between a STAR and an approach. CLR then a left key deletes that line. A gap cannot be deleted after a (VECT) leg: drop the next waypoint onto the (VECT) or delete the (VECT).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DISCONTINUITY and DELETING A WAYPOINT

fp_perf.title: Weights and cruise altitude
fp_perf.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 PERF INIT and section 4 Weight and balance; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class PerfInitPage

steps.text: Press the PERF key.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class PerfMenuPage: perfInitLink on line 1 left

steps.text: Press LSK L1 (<PERF INIT).
steps.why: PERF INIT is where you tell the FMS how heavy the aircraft is. The take-off and landing speeds use these numbers, not the weights of the simulator.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class PerfMenuPage: perfInitLink on line 1 left

steps.text: Type the number of people and their average weight in lb, for example 6/180, and press LSK L2 (PASS/WT). Count the pilots too.
steps.why: BOW is the empty weight without people, bags or fuel. The model does not include a pilot in it, so the pilots must be in this number. With only a count (for example 4) the FMS uses 170 lb each.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 PERF INIT (PASS/WT) and section 4 (pilots are not in the BOW); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class PassengerDataFormat

steps.text: Type the baggage and cargo weight and press LSK L3 (CARGO).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 PERF INIT (CARGO)

steps.text: Type the planned cruise altitude, for example 20000 or FL350, and press LSK R1 (CRZ ALT).
steps.why: The community checklist lists typical cruise altitudes by trip distance: 0 to 99 NM 4,000 to 12,000 ft; 100 to 199 NM 12,000 to 24,000 ft; 200 to 299 NM 23,000 to 31,000 ft; 300 to 499 NM 30,000 to 39,000 ft; 500 to 999 NM 38,000 to 43,000 ft; 1,000 NM and more 41,000 to 45,000 ft (Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), TYPICAL CRUISE ALTITUDES).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 PERF INIT (CRZ ALT: whole number, FLXX or FXXX); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class AltitudeInputFormat (accepts up to 45000 ft)

steps.text: Check SENSED FUEL, ZFW and GWT on the page.
steps.why: ZFW is the weight without fuel, GWT the total weight now. Limits: maximum take-off weight 17,110 lb, maximum zero fuel weight 12,500 lb (the ZFW turns yellow above it), maximum landing weight 15,660 lb. If you change the fuel in the sim, leave PERF INIT and open it again to refresh SENSED FUEL.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 PERF INIT (SENSED FUEL, ZFW, GWT); MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 2 Weight limits

fp_takeoff.title: Take-off data and speeds
fp_takeoff.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TAKEOFF; MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff and landing V-speeds; sim file asobo-aircraft-cj4, panel/Instruments/WT21/Plugins/CJ4FmcPlugins.js, class CJ4TakeoffRefPage

steps.text: Press the PERF key.
steps.source: sim file asobo-aircraft-cj4, panel/Instruments/WT21/Plugins/CJ4FmcPlugins.js, class CJ4PerfMenuPageExtension (<TAKEOFF on line 3 left); MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 (a departure runway must be selected through DEP/ARR first)

steps.text: Press LSK L3 (<TAKEOFF).
steps.why: This is the TAKEOFF REF page, page 1 of 3.
steps.source: sim file asobo-aircraft-cj4, panel/Instruments/WT21/Plugins/CJ4FmcPlugins.js, class CJ4PerfMenuPageExtension (<TAKEOFF on line 3 left); MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 (a departure runway must be selected through DEP/ARR first)

steps.text: Type the wind from the ATIS, for example 240/6, and press LSK R1 (WIND).
steps.why: Leave it blank and the FMS assumes calm wind. RWY WIND then shows the headwind (H) or tailwind (T) and crosswind (L or R) components.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TAKEOFF (WIND); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WindFormat (direction 0 to 360, speed up to 100)

steps.text: Type the outside air temperature in degrees C and press LSK R2 (OAT).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TAKEOFF (OAT, required for the speeds); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class TemperatureFormat (whole number, up to 54, minus sign for below zero)

steps.text: Type the altimeter setting and press LSK R3 (QNH).
steps.why: 30.01 inHg can be typed as 3001.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TAKEOFF (QNH, required for the speeds); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class PerfQnhFormat (29.92, 2992, or 4 digits below 2000 as hPa)

steps.text: Check RWY COND (line L5): DRY or WET. Press LSK L5 to change it.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TAKEOFF (RWY COND: a WET runway increases the take-off distance)

steps.text: Press the NEXT page key. Check T/O FLAPS (line L2): 15 in most cases, 0 if heavy or hot and high. Press LSK L2 to change it.
steps.why: The flaps you set later on the pedestal must match this choice. A/I (line L1) is the anti-ice setting for the calculation: ON slightly increases the take-off distance; the CJ4 does not model degraded engine performance with anti-ice (guide).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TAKEOFF page 2/3 (T/O FLAPS selectable between 0 and 15)

steps.text: Compare TOFL with the runway length on line L4 (TOFL/RWxx), and check TOW/GWT/MTOW above it.
steps.why: TOFL is the take-off field length the aircraft needs. If it is longer than the runway, choose another runway, reduce the weight or review the data.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TAKEOFF page 2/3 (TOFL: from the start of the roll to 35 ft above the runway)

steps.text: Read V1, VR, V2 and VT in the right column.
steps.why: V1: speed after which a take-off should not be aborted. VR: rotation speed. V2: safe speed for single-engine operation after an engine failure. VT: single-engine enroute climb speed, always 140 KIAS.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TAKEOFF page 2/3

steps.text: Press LSK R6 (SEND>) to send the speeds to the PFD.
steps.why: Speeds sent by the FMS are magenta on the PFD, speeds you change by hand are cyan (guide).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TAKEOFF page 2/3 (IN PROGRESS then COMPLETE, shown in magenta below the speed tape)

fp_end.title: Flight plan ready
fp_end.text: Position, route, departure, weights and take-off speeds are set. Next, open the topic Before taxi and taxi.

rv_which.title: What do you want to set?
rv_which.text: What do you want to set?
rv_which.help: The frequencies are entered on the TUN page of the CDU. LSK means line select key: L1 is the top key on the left of the CDU screen and R6 the bottom key on the right.

choices.label: A NAV radio frequency (VOR or ILS)

rv_com.title: COM radio
rv_com.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TUN (TUNE 1/2); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class TunePage and ComFrequencyFormat

steps.text: Press the TUN key.
steps.why: The TUNE page holds all radio frequencies and the transponder code.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TUN

steps.text: Type the new frequency, for example 124.85 or 2485, and press LSK L1 (COM1) or R1 (COM2).
steps.why: The new frequency becomes active and the old active frequency moves to RECALL (the line below).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TUN (shorthand: omit the 1 or the decimal point); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class ComFrequencyFormat (118 to 137 MHz)

steps.text: To swap the active and RECALL frequencies, clear the scratchpad and press LSK L2 (COM1) or R2 (COM2).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TUN (RECALL: press LSK 2L/2R to swap); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class TunePage.com1StandbyField (empty scratchpad swaps)

steps.text: On the audio panel, make sure the radio you want to talk on is the transmit radio and its knob is not muted.
steps.why: You can transmit on one radio at a time and listen to both. In the sim, a knob turned all the way left is maximum volume and a knob pointing straight up is muted, and you can mute the radio you transmit on. In DISPATCH only COM1 is available (guide).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 Audio control panel (COM 1/2)

rv_nav.title: NAV radio
rv_nav.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TUN; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class TunePage and NavFrequencyFormat

steps.text: Press the TUN key.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TUN

steps.text: Type the VOR or ILS frequency (for example 111.10 or 11110) or the 3-letter VOR name, and press LSK L3 (NAV1) or R3 (NAV2).
steps.why: The field then shows MAN: the radio stays on the frequency you chose. AUTO means the FMS tunes it. To go back to AUTO, press CLR with an empty scratchpad (the word DELETE appears) and then LSK L3. The guide says NAV control is not available while the avionics switch is in DISPATCH.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class NavFrequencyFormat.parse (108 to 117.95 MHz in 50 kHz steps, or a nearby VOR identifier)

rv_xpdr.title: Transponder
rv_xpdr.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TUN and ATC CONTROL; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class TunePage and TransponderCodeFormat

steps.text: Press the TUN key.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TUN

steps.text: Type the 4-digit code from ATC and press LSK L5 (ATC1).
steps.why: Digits 8 and 9 do not exist in a transponder code (guide).
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class TransponderCodeFormat (4 digits, each 0 to 7)

steps.text: Set TCAS MODE (line R5) to TA or RA, not STBY. Press LSK R5 to change it.
steps.why: The guide says that in the sim TA/RA basically just turns the transponder ON (Mode C), also for online clients. Resolution advisories are not modelled.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TUN (TCAS MODE: TA/RA turns the transponder on, Mode C); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class TunePage.tcasModeSwitch (TA, RA, STBY)

rv_baro.title: Altimeter setting
rv_baro.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 7 DCP BARO; MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 7 DCP BARO; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAXI item 13, AFTER TAKEOFF item 10, DESCENT item 3

steps.text: Turn the BARO knob on the display control panel above the PFD until the altimeter setting under the altitude tape matches the local value.
steps.why: Below the transition altitude use the local altimeter setting (QNH). The catalog notes: one step of the knob changes the setting by about 0.3 hPa.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 7 DCP BARO (sets the altimeter display below the altitude indicator)

steps.text: To set the standard setting, press the BARO knob.
steps.why: Use standard pressure at and above the transition altitude (general airmanship, the sources give no value). The checklist asks you to set and cross-check the altimeters after take-off and again in the descent. In the catalog tests the press changed the setting from 1013.25 to 1013.24 hPa and the second press changed it back; the STD state itself could not be read, so check the altimeter display.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 7 DCP BARO (pressing the BARO knob sets 29.92 STD, or 1013 STD with hPa)

rv_done.title: Done
rv_done.text: The setting is entered. Open this topic again for another radio or setting.

bt_ground.title: Where is the aircraft?
bt_ground.text: Is the aircraft on the ground?

bt_air.title: Not on the ground
bt_air.text: Taxiing is a ground procedure. In flight, use the topics Climb and cruise, Descent and approach or Landing.
bt_air.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 3 Normal procedures (order of the procedures)

bt_eng.title: Engines
bt_eng.help: The checks before taxi come after the engine start.

auto.code: (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:2, Bool) +

bt_noeng.title: Start the engines first
bt_noeng.text: Open the topic Start the engines and come back when both engines run.
bt_noeng.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: the sim's checklist ends with the page AFTER STARTING ENGINE; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), START comes before BEFORE TAXI

bt_check.title: Before taxi
bt_check.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAXI; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 Systems

steps.text: Make sure the avionics master switch is ON.
steps.why: DISPATCH powers only the left MFD and the left FMS (guide): the PFD stays dark until the switch is ON.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAXI item 1; CJ4_Checklist.xml: Avionics_Bus_Switch_On, value 0 after the engine start

steps.text: Set the climate control selector to NORM.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAXI item 2

steps.text: Press the passenger safety (PASS SAFETY) light button ON.
steps.why: This plays the safety message over the PA. On the real aircraft it lights the seat belt, no smoking and exit signs (guide).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAXI item 3; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 SAFETY

steps.text: Check the three trims: aileron, rudder and elevator.
steps.why: The checklists give no trim value. The trim indications are on the engine display of the MFD. After rotation you trim for 10 degrees nose up (guide).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAXI item 4 (CHECK/SET) and BEFORE TAKEOFF item 6 (SET FOR TAKEOFF)

steps.text: Check that the flight controls move freely and the right way.
steps.why: Technique: move the yoke and the pedals and look at the surfaces. The checklist only says FREE/CORRECT.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAXI item 5 (FLIGHT CONTROLS FREE/CORRECT)

steps.text: Check that the speed brake / ground spoiler lever is fully back.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAXI item 6 and BEFORE TAKEOFF item 5 (SPEED BRAKES 0%)

steps.text: Check that take-off data is set and the speeds are on the PFD.
steps.why: V1, VR and V2 show in magenta below the speed tape after SEND on the TAKEOFF REF page. If they are missing, open the topic Set up the flight plan in the FMS.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAXI item 10 (TAKEOFF DATA CONFIRM/SET); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TAKEOFF

steps.text: Set the altimeter to the local setting and check it.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAXI item 13 (ALTIMETER SET/CHECK)

bt_flaps_q.title: Take-off flaps
bt_flaps_q.text: What does T/O FLAPS say on page 2 of the TAKEOFF REF page?
bt_flaps_q.help: Flaps 15 is almost always used for take-off. Flaps 0 is used when the aircraft is heavy and/or the departure airport is hot and high (guide). Find it with PERF, then <TAKEOFF, then NEXT.

bt_fl15.title: Flaps 15
bt_fl15.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAXI item 7 (FLAPS CHECK/SET); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TAKEOFF page 2/3; sim file asobo-aircraft-cj4, flight_model.cfg, [FLAPS.0] positions 0, 15, 35

steps.text: Set the flaps to 15.
steps.why: The flap handle has three positions: 0, 15 and 35 degrees.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAXI item 7; sim file asobo-aircraft-cj4, flight_model.cfg, flaps-position.1 = 15 (handle index 1)

bt_fl0.title: Flaps 0
bt_fl0.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAXI item 7 (FLAPS CHECK/SET); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TAKEOFF page 2/3

steps.text: Make sure the flaps are at 0.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAXI item 7; sim file asobo-aircraft-cj4, flight_model.cfg, flaps-position.0 = 0 (handle index 0)

bt_taxi.title: Taxi
bt_taxi.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), TAXI; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 Exterior lights

steps.text: Turn the taxi light ON.
steps.why: The guide: the taxi lights and the landing lights are the same lights at different intensities. Taxi is the normal intensity. The logo lights are generally used at night from engine start to engine shutdown.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), TAXI item 1 (EXTERIOR LIGHTS AS REQUIRED); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 TAXI

steps.text: Make sure the parking brake is released.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), TAXI item 3; CJ4_Checklist.xml: Parking_Brake_Release

steps.text: Check the brakes as you start to roll.
steps.why: Technique: a gentle brake application in the first metres. The checklist only says CHECK.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), TAXI item 4 (BRAKES CHECK)

steps.text: Check the nose wheel steering.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), TAXI item 5 (NOSE WHEEL STEERING CHECK)

steps.text: Check the flight instruments in the first turns.
steps.why: Technique: the attitude and heading indications on the PFD should follow your turns.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), TAXI item 6 (FLIGHT INSTRUMENTS CHECK)

bt_done.title: Taxi checks done
bt_done.text: Taxi to the runway. Next, open the topic Take off.

to_ground.title: Where is the aircraft?
to_ground.text: Is the aircraft on the ground?

to_air.title: Already flying
to_air.text: You are already airborne. Open the topic Climb and cruise. If you are still low with the gear down, its first part (just taken off) lists the gear, flaps and yaw damper steps.
to_air.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure (p. 3-2)

to_pre.title: Before take-off
to_pre.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAKEOFF; MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure (p. 3-2)

steps.text: Check the flaps are at the T/O FLAPS value (0 or 15).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAKEOFF item 4 (FLAPS CHECK/SET)

steps.text: Check the speed brakes are at 0 %.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAKEOFF item 5 (SPEED BRAKES 0%)

steps.text: Check the three trims are set for take-off.
steps.why: The checklist gives no trim value.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAKEOFF item 6 (TRIMS (3) SET FOR TAKEOFF)

steps.text: Brief the take-off.
steps.why: General airmanship, a checklist item without a procedure in the sources.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAKEOFF item 7 (CREW BRIEFING COMPLETE)

steps.text: Set the TCAS mode to TA or RA on the TUN page (line R5).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAKEOFF item 8 (TCAS TA/RA); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class TunePage.tcasModeSwitch

steps.text: Turn the pitot/static heat ON.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAKEOFF item 13 (PITOT/STATIC HEAT BUTTONS ON)

steps.text: Check the take-off speeds are on the PFD.
steps.why: If V1, VR and V2 are missing, press SEND on page 2 of TAKEOFF REF.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TAKEOFF page 2/3 (magenta below the speed tape)

to_line.title: Line up
to_line.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 Exterior lights; MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure (p. 3-2)

steps.text: Turn the strobe lights ON.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 STROBE (on when entering an active runway for crossing or for take-off, left on until exiting the runway after landing)

steps.text: Turn the landing lights ON.
steps.why: The pulse light system, if you use it, overrides the steady landing lights. It must be OFF for all night ground operations and for night flight below 300 ft AGL (guide).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 LNDG (highest intensity, most commonly used for take-off and landing, and below 10,000 ft)

steps.text: Press the TOGA button when you enter the runway.
steps.why: The flight director then commands 10 degrees nose up and straight ahead. The scoreboard at the top of the PFD shows TO. The guide says the throttle button was not working and suggests binding the AUTO THROTTLE TO GA event; this sim's cockpit file defines the throttle button and a shortcut on the fire bottle under the L ENG FIRE button.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure (p. 3-2: when entering runway, enable TOGA); sim file asobo-aircraft-cj4, model/CJ4_Cockpit.xml (TOGA_PUSH sends AUTO_THROTTLE_TO_GA from the throttle button)

to_style.title: Take-off style
to_style.text: How do you want to take off?
to_style.help: Performance is generally the same. For short runways a static take-off is preferred so enough runway stays inside the safety margins (guide).

choices.label: Rolling: do not stop after lining up

to_static.title: Hold the brakes
to_static.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure (p. 3-2); Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), TAKEOFF item 3

steps.text: Hold the wheel brakes.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure (for a static take-off, hold the brakes)

steps.text: Advance the thrust levers to the TO detent, then release the brakes as the engines spool up.
steps.why: The next page has the thrust lever step: skip it if you already did it here. This app's lever event only goes to idle (10 or less) or to full power (11 or more): use your throttle hardware or the standard THROTTLE axis for anything in between.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), TAKEOFF items 1 and 3 (THROTTLES TAKEOFF, BRAKES RELEASE)

to_roll.title: Take-off roll and climb-out
to_roll.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure (p. 3-2 and 3-3); Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), TAKEOFF and AFTER TAKEOFF/CLIMB

steps.text: Push both thrust levers fully forward to the TO (take-off) detent.
steps.why: The engine display on the MFD shows the FADEC mode beside the N1 gauge. This app's lever event only goes to idle (10 or less) or to full power (11 or more): use your throttle hardware or the standard THROTTLE axis for anything in between.
steps.warn: Maximum sustained take-off power is 5 minutes in total per engine start/stop cycle (guide, engine limits).
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure (advance throttle to TO detent, full forward); Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), TAKEOFF item 1

steps.text: At VR (from the TAKEOFF REF page), rotate.
steps.why: If you must stop, do it before V1: after V1 a take-off should not be aborted (guide).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), TAKEOFF item 4 (CONTROL WHEEL ROTATE AT VR); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TAKEOFF page 2/3

steps.text: After rotation, raise the nose to 10 degrees and trim as needed.
steps.why: The flight director in TO mode commands the same 10 degrees (guide).
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure (after rotation, increase pitch to 10 degrees nose up and trim accordingly)

steps.text: When you pass V2 + 10 knots, raise the landing gear.
steps.why: V2 is on the TAKEOFF REF page and on the speed tape.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure (retract gear and set FLAPS 0 after accelerating through V2 + 10); Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER TAKEOFF item 1

steps.text: Set the flaps to 0.
steps.why: Skip it if the T/O FLAPS value was 0.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER TAKEOFF item 2

steps.text: Turn the yaw damper ON.
steps.why: YD appears in the autopilot status area of the scoreboard (guide). The yaw damper must be engaged after lift-off.
steps.warn: The earliest height for the yaw damper or the autopilot after take-off is 300 ft above the ground. The button toggles: if YD already shows on the PFD, leave it.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure (engage the yaw damper after retracting flaps); Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER TAKEOFF item 4

steps.text: Passing 1,000 ft above the ground, pull both thrust levers back to the CLB detent.
steps.why: The FADEC manages the power during the whole climb (guide). This app's lever event only goes to idle (10 or less) or to full power (11 or more): use your throttle hardware or the standard THROTTLE axis for anything in between.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure (passing 1,000 ft AGL reduce power to CLB setting detent); Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER TAKEOFF item 3

to_done.title: Airborne
to_done.text: The gear and flaps are up, the yaw damper is on and the engines are at climb power. Next, open the topic Climb and cruise.

cc_air.title: Where is the aircraft?
cc_air.text: Is the aircraft in the air?

choices.label: No, it is on the ground

cc_ground.title: Still on the ground
cc_ground.text: Take off first: open the topic Take off.
cc_ground.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure

cc_phase.title: Where are you in the flight?
cc_phase.help: If the landing gear handle is still down, the guide starts with the gear, flaps and yaw damper.

choices.label: I am at my cruise altitude

cc_after.title: After take-off
cc_after.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER TAKEOFF/CLIMB; MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure

steps.text: Raise the landing gear.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER TAKEOFF item 1

steps.text: Set the flaps to 0.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER TAKEOFF item 2

steps.text: Pull both thrust levers back to the CLB detent.
steps.why: Skip it if you already did it. This app's lever event only goes to idle (10 or less) or to full power (11 or more): use your throttle hardware or the standard THROTTLE axis for anything in between.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure (passing 1,000 ft AGL); Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER TAKEOFF item 3

steps.text: Turn the yaw damper ON.
steps.warn: Not below 300 ft above the ground. The button toggles: if YD already shows on the PFD, leave it.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER TAKEOFF item 4

steps.text: Turn the landing lights off above 10,000 ft if you do not need them.
steps.why: The sources say 'as required' and name below 10,000 ft as a common use.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER TAKEOFF item 8 (LANDING LIGHTS AS REQUIRED); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 LNDG (most commonly used for take-off, landing and below 10,000 ft)

steps.text: Check the cabin pressurization.
steps.why: A checklist item. The sources do not say where to read it.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER TAKEOFF item 9 (PRESSURIZATION CHECK)

steps.text: Set the altimeters and cross-check them.
steps.why: Pressing the BARO knob sets the standard setting (29.92 or 1013).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER TAKEOFF item 10 (ALTIMETERS SET/CROSSCHECK); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 7 DCP BARO

cc_ap.title: Climb with the autopilot
cc_ap.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure and Climb procedure (p. 3-2, 3-4); MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6

steps.text: Turn the ALT knob to the altitude you were cleared to.
steps.why: The knob is on the flight guidance panel (FGP). Each click is 100 ft (catalog). The autopilot captures this altitude: the scoreboard shows ALTS CAP and then ALT.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure (set target initial climb altitude with the ALT knob on the FGP)

steps.text: Make sure the flight director is on (FD button).
steps.why: The catalog tests of the mode buttons were done with the flight director on.
steps.warn: The FD button toggles: if the flight director bars are already shown, leave it.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 FD

steps.text: Press FLC.
steps.why: FLC holds a speed with pitch only: the nose goes up to slow down and down to speed up. The CJ4 has no autothrottle, so you set the thrust.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure (engage FLC mode); MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 FLC

steps.text: Set 240 knots with the SPEED knob.
steps.why: The autopilot switches to Mach 0.64 by itself at about FL300. The selected speed marker shows on the PFD only while FLC is the active vertical mode (guide).
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure (set target speed to 240 KIAS) and Climb procedure

cc_lat_q.title: Lateral mode
cc_lat_q.text: How are you flying the departure?
cc_lat_q.help: The guide: engage HDG or NAV depending on the departure procedure.

cc_nav.title: Follow the flight plan
cc_nav.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 NAV; MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 7 DCP NAV

steps.text: Check the PFD shows FMS1 as the navigation source. If not, press the NAV button on the display control panel above the PFD.
steps.why: With the FMS as the source, the flight guidance follows the flight plan.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 7 DCP (NAV button toggles between the active source and the preset: FMS1, VOR1/LOC1, VOR2/LOC2)

steps.text: Press NAV on the flight guidance panel.
steps.why: The plane stays in its current mode until it is close enough to the FMS course. Then LNV1 becomes the active lateral mode on the scoreboard. In this app's tests, pressing NAV with no navigation source engaged nothing.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 NAV (with the FMS as the source, pressing NAV arms LNV)

cc_hdg.title: Fly a heading
cc_hdg.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 HDG

steps.text: Turn the HDG knob to the heading ATC gave you.
steps.why: Each click moves the heading bug by 1 degree (catalog). Pressing the HDG knob sets the bug to the present heading (guide).
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 HDG (selected heading is changed with the HDG knob)

steps.text: Press HDG.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 HDG (enables heading hold)

cc_apon.title: Engage the autopilot
cc_apon.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure (p. 3-2); MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6

steps.text: Engage the autopilot with the AP button.
steps.why: The autopilot at once follows the modes you chose. Some pilots hand-fly to 240 knots first so that FLC does not pitch down to accelerate. The yaw damper is always on when the autopilot is on.
steps.warn: Never below 300 ft above the ground after take-off. The AP button toggles.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure (from about 200 KIAS you can enable the autopilot, a personal choice); section 6 Autopilot limitations (300 ft AGL minimum)

cc_climb.title: Climb
cc_climb.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Climb procedure (p. 3-4); MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 Flight guidance system display

steps.text: Watch the speed: FLC holds 240 knots, then Mach 0.64.
steps.why: The FADEC manages climb power up to the cruise altitude. Typical climb rates: 3,000 to 5,000 fpm below 20,000 ft, 2,000 to 3,000 fpm in the 20,000s, about 2,000 fpm decreasing in the 30,000s (guide).
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Climb procedure (FLC at 240 KIAS / M0.64, switched automatically)

steps.text: When you reach the selected altitude, check the scoreboard shows ALT.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 Flight guidance system display (ALT: the plane has captured a baro altitude)

cc_cruise.title: Cruise
cc_cruise.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Cruise procedure (p. 3-4); Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), CRUISE; MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 2 Speed limits

steps.text: Set the thrust levers for the cruise speed you want.
steps.why: Speeds are managed by the pilot, up to MMO / VMO.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Cruise procedure (any throttle setting besides TO can be used; no CRU detent; no autothrottle)

steps.text: Stay inside the speed limits.
steps.warn: Above 27,884 ft: Mach 0.77. Between 8,000 and 27,884 ft: 305 KIAS (VMO). Below 8,000 ft: 260 KIAS (VMN).
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 2 Speed limits

steps.text: Press the PERF key.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Cruise procedure (monitor fuel flow, range and time to reserve on the FMS PERF pages); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FuelMgmtPage

steps.text: Press LSK R1 (FUEL MGMT>) and read the fuel, fuel flow, range and time to reserve.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Cruise procedure (monitor fuel flow, range and time to reserve on the FMS PERF pages); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FuelMgmtPage

steps.text: Check the pressurization and the ice protection and use the ice protection as required.
steps.why: Checklist items. The sources give no temperature or icing criteria.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), CRUISE items 2 and 3

cc_done.title: Cruising
cc_done.text: You are level at cruise altitude. When it is time to come down, open the topic Descent and approach.

da_air.title: Where is the aircraft?
da_air.text: Is the aircraft in the air?

choices.label: No, it is on the ground

da_ground.title: On the ground
da_ground.text: The descent and approach are flown in the air. For the ground, open Before taxi and taxi or After landing and shutdown.
da_ground.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Descent procedure and Approach and landing

da_arr.title: Arrival and approach in the FMS
da_arr.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing (p. 3-5); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEP ARR, ARRIVAL, VISUAL APPROACHES; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class DepArrPage

steps.text: Check the destination weather and, when it fits, ask ATC which approach to expect.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing (p. 3-5)

steps.text: Press the DEP ARR key.
steps.why: More than 50 NM from the destination, or halfway to it, DEP ARR opens the ACT ARRIVAL page by itself (guide). LSK means line select key: L1 is the top key on the left of the CDU screen and R6 the bottom key on the right.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEP ARR

steps.text: If the DEP/ARR INDEX shows, press LSK R2 (ARR>).
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class DepArrPage.getIndexTemplate and onHandleSelectKey (right key, line 2)

steps.text: If ATC gave you a STAR, choose it on the left, then its transition.
steps.why: STAR means standard terminal arrival route. You can choose a STAR before an approach or runway, because these are usually only assigned within 50 NM. Some STARs do not show all their fixes until a runway or approach is chosen. NEXT and PREV show more pages.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 ARRIVAL

steps.text: Choose the approach on the right (APPROACHES), then its transition if one is listed.
steps.why: For a visual approach, look for the entries that start with RW followed by the runway number (use NEXT to find them) and choose one. VIS RWY EXT then appears: an extension point out from the runway, 5 NM by default, up to 25 NM. Press a green (chosen) item again to remove it.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 ARRIVAL and VISUAL APPROACHES; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class DepArrPageController (right column of the ARRIVAL page, visual approaches shown as RW)

steps.text: Press EXEC.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEPART (MOD until EXEC)

steps.text: Press LEGS and check the waypoints, the restrictions and the MISSED APPR line.
steps.why: If an instrument approach is loaded, its missed approach follows the runway in the list (guide).
steps.warn: Do not change the approach after you have started it: this can cause FMS errors and force you back to the initial approach fix in LNAV (guide).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 LEGS and MISSED APPROACH

da_perf.title: Landing speeds and minimums
da_perf.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing (p. 3-5); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 APPROACH; sim file asobo-aircraft-cj4, panel/Instruments/WT21/Plugins/CJ4FmcPlugins.js, class CJ4ApproachRefPage

steps.text: Press the PERF key.
steps.source: sim file asobo-aircraft-cj4, panel/Instruments/WT21/Plugins/CJ4FmcPlugins.js, class CJ4PerfMenuPageExtension (APPROACH> on line 3 right); MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 (an approach and a runway must be chosen in DEP/ARR first)

steps.text: Press LSK R3 (APPROACH>).
steps.why: This is the APPROACH REF page, page 1 of 3.
steps.source: sim file asobo-aircraft-cj4, panel/Instruments/WT21/Plugins/CJ4FmcPlugins.js, class CJ4PerfMenuPageExtension (APPROACH> on line 3 right); MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 (an approach and a runway must be chosen in DEP/ARR first)

steps.text: Type the wind at the destination, for example 240/6, and press LSK R1 (WIND).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 APPROACH (WIND)

steps.text: Type the temperature at the destination in degrees C and press LSK R2 (OAT).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 APPROACH (OAT, required); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class TemperatureFormat

steps.text: Type the destination altimeter setting and press LSK R3 (QNH).
steps.why: 30.01 inHg can be typed as 3001.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 APPROACH (QNH, required); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class PerfQnhFormat

steps.text: Check RWY COND (line L6): DRY or WET. Press LSK L6 to change it.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 APPROACH (a WET runway leads to a longer landing distance)

steps.text: Press the NEXT page key. Check LW/GWT/MLW and LFL against the runway length.
steps.why: MLW is the maximum landing weight, 15,660 lb. If LFL is longer than the runway, review the approach, the runway or the weight. LDG FACTOR (line L5) adds a margin to the distance for emergencies (1.00, 1.25, 1.67 or 1.92).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 APPROACH page 2/3 (LFL: required landing field length)

steps.text: Read VREF and VAPP in the right column.
steps.why: VREF is 1.3 times the stall speed in the landing configuration for the weight. VAPP is VREF + 7 knots and does not include the wind.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 APPROACH page 2/3

steps.text: Press LSK R6 (SEND>) to send the speeds to the PFD.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 APPROACH (send the speeds to the PFD); sim file asobo-aircraft-cj4, panel/Instruments/WT21/Plugins/CJ4FmcPlugins.js, class CJ4ApproachRefPage.sendVSpeeds

steps.text: In wind or gusts, raise VAPP by half the steady headwind plus the gust value, never by more than 15 knots. Use the REFS MENU button above the PFD.
steps.why: Speeds you change by hand are cyan on the PFD, speeds sent by the FMS are magenta. A changed speed must be enabled with a check mark before it shows on the speed tape again (guide).
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff and landing V-speeds and section 7 REFS MENU

steps.text: Set the BARO minimums on the REFS menu.
steps.why: The CJ4 is certified for CAT I ILS and LPV/WAAS approaches with minimums not lower than 200 ft AGL. BARO minimums must be used for every approach. RNP AR approaches are not authorized.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 7 REFS MENU (MINIMUMS BARO, 0 to 14,000 ft) and section 2 Approach types; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), APPROACH item 4

da_desc.title: Plan the descent
da_desc.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Descent procedure (p. 3-4); Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), DESCENT

steps.text: Work out where to start down: (altitude - airport elevation) / 1,000 x 3 gives the distance in NM.
steps.why: Example from the guide: cruise at 45,000 ft, landing at 5,000 ft: 40,000 / 1,000 x 3 = 120 NM before the airport.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Descent procedure (top of descent for a 3 degree path)

steps.text: For a 3 degree path, descend at about ground speed x 5 feet per minute.
steps.why: Example: 450 knots ground speed gives 2,250 fpm. Rates up to 3,000 fpm are allowed, especially from cruise altitude.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Descent procedure

steps.text: Turn the ALT knob to the first altitude ATC gave you.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 ALT

steps.text: Set the cabin pressurization for the landing airport elevation.
steps.why: A checklist item. The sources do not say how to set it.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), DESCENT item 1 (PRESSURIZATION VERIFY/SET LDG ELEV)

steps.text: Set the altimeters and cross-check them.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), DESCENT item 3

steps.text: Set the exterior lights as required and use ice protection as required.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), DESCENT items 2 and 4

da_desc_q.title: Descent mode
da_desc_q.text: How do you want to fly the descent?
da_desc_q.help: The guide: you can use FLC, VS or VNAV. VS lets you hit altitude restrictions more exactly but you must watch power and speed all the time. With FLC you set a speed target and use the thrust for the descent rate.

choices.label: VNAV: follow the flight plan altitudes

da_vnav.title: Descent with VNAV
da_vnav.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 VNAV and VNAV operation (p. 6-5 to 6-7)

steps.text: Check that the LEGS page shows the altitude restrictions of the STAR and approach.
steps.why: The CJ4 FMS shows only restrictions that are loaded or typed in. It does not show predicted altitudes at each fix. That is normal: VNAV still flies the computed path. There is no need to enter a restriction for every fix.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 VNAV operation

steps.text: Press VNAV.
steps.why: PATH is armed when you are within 1,000 ft of the computed path. If the armed VNAV message says the path cannot be captured because you are too far above it, descend to the path with VS or FLC first. The angle is set on the VNAV SETUP page.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 VNAV (in descent, PATH is the default mode when no other vertical mode is chosen; the default descent angle is 3 degrees)

steps.text: Manage the speed with the thrust levers yourself.
steps.why: The PFD shows TOD about 5 to 10 seconds before the descent starts, as a reminder that you will need to change the thrust.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 VNAV PATH (VNAV does not adjust the engine thrust)

steps.text: If VNAV does not do what you expect, turn it off and on again.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 1 Other known issues

steps.text: Be at 250 knots by 10,000 ft.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Descent procedure (allow time to slow to 250 KIAS by 10,000 ft)

da_vs.title: Descent with VS
da_vs.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Descent procedure and section 6 VS

steps.text: Press VS.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 VS (the plane adjusts pitch to meet the selected vertical speed)

steps.text: Set the descent rate with the VS wheel.
steps.why: Remember the rule of thumb: ground speed x 5 gives about 3 degrees. Each click changes the selected rate by 100 fpm, only while VS is engaged (catalog).
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 VS (selected with the vertical speed/pitch wheel, UP and DOWN)

steps.text: Watch the power and the speed all the time.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Descent procedure (VS: you need to constantly monitor your power settings and speed)

steps.text: Be at 250 knots by 10,000 ft and do not descend steeper than 3 degrees below 250 knots (about 1,250 fpm at 250 knots).
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Descent procedure

da_flc.title: Descent with FLC
da_flc.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Descent procedure and section 6 FLC

steps.text: Press FLC.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 FLC (the plane adjusts pitch to keep the selected speed: it pitches down to gain speed)

steps.text: Set a speed below VMO / MMO with the SPEED knob.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Descent procedure (set a target speed not above Vne/MMO)

steps.text: Use the thrust levers to get the descent rate you want.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Descent procedure and section 6 FLC note (no autothrottle: speed in FLC is controlled only by pitch)

steps.text: Be at 250 knots by 10,000 ft and do not descend steeper than 3 degrees below 250 knots (about 1,250 fpm at 250 knots).
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Descent procedure

da_type.title: Approach type
da_type.help: The CJ4 is certified for CAT I ILS and LPV/WAAS approaches, with barometric minimums not lower than 200 ft AGL (guide).

choices.label: RNAV / GPS approach from the FMS

da_ils.title: ILS approach
da_ils.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing (p. 3-5) and section 6 APPR; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WT21NavToNavManager; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), APPROACH

steps.text: Check that NAV1 on the TUN page shows the ILS frequency from the chart.
steps.why: Within about 31 NM of the destination, with the ILS in the flight plan and the FMS as the navigation source, the FMS tunes the localizer itself: the message LOC WILL BE TUNED shows and about 30 seconds later NAV1 and NAV2 are on the ILS frequency (from the sim's FMS software). The guide's tip to read the course on the ARR DATA page does not work here: ARR DATA is greyed out in this sim's FMS.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing (confirm the proper ILS frequency is set in the TUN page for NAV1)

steps.text: Slow to 200 knots or less before you start the approach.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing

steps.text: Set the flaps to 15.
steps.why: Maximum speed with flaps 15 is 200 KIAS (guide).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), APPROACH item 8; sim file asobo-aircraft-cj4, flight_model.cfg, flaps-position.1 = 15 (handle index 1)

steps.text: Press APPR on the flight guidance panel.
steps.why: When the localizer is captured, APPR LOC becomes the active lateral mode, and when the glideslope is captured, GS becomes the active vertical mode. While the localizer is armed, the PFD shows a ghost needle; the FMS then switches the navigation source to NAV1 by itself (from the sim's FMS software). In this app's tests, pressing APPR with no navigation source engaged nothing.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 APPR (during an ILS approach it arms APPR LOC and GS)

steps.text: Be at 160 knots or less at the final approach fix, and at VAPP for a precision approach.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing

steps.text: Check the scoreboard: LOC, then GS.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 Flight guidance system display (armed and active modes)

da_rnav.title: RNAV approach
da_rnav.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing and section 6 APPR; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 7 PFD HSI and section 1 Other known issues

steps.text: Make sure the FMS is the navigation source on the PFD. If not, press the NAV button on the display control panel above the PFD.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 7 DCP NAV (FMS1, VOR1/LOC1, VOR2/LOC2)

steps.text: Slow to 200 knots or less and set the flaps to 15.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), APPROACH item 8

steps.text: Press APPR on the flight guidance panel.
steps.why: When the FMS course is captured, APPR LNV becomes active. When the vertical glide path is captured, GP becomes active. For an LPV approach the PFD shows LPV APPR before the final approach fix (0.02 NM accuracy, guide). In this app's tests, pressing APPR with no navigation source engaged nothing.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 APPR (during an RNAV approach it arms APPR LNV and GP)

steps.text: Be at 160 knots or less at the final approach fix, and at VAPP for a precision approach.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing

steps.text: Be ready to fly the approach by hand if the autopilot overshoots a tight turn.
steps.why: The guide recommends hand-flying with the lateral and vertical guidance in that case.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 1 Other known issues (autopilot bank rate limits can cause overshoot on certain RNP approaches)

da_visual.title: Visual approach
da_visual.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 VISUAL APPROACHES; MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing

steps.text: Fly the visual approach only in visual conditions.
steps.warn: A visual approach must not be used in instrument meteorological conditions as a substitute for an instrument approach.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 VISUAL APPROACHES

steps.text: If you want a pattern to follow, use the RX waypoint on the LEGS page and make your own downwind, base and final waypoints.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 VISUAL APPROACHES (the runway extension shows as RX on the LEGS page; you can build custom waypoints from it, or delete RX)

steps.text: Slow to 200 knots or less and set the flaps to 15.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), APPROACH item 8

steps.text: Fly the approach speed (VAPP) on final.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff and landing V-speeds

da_done.title: Established for landing
da_done.text: You are configured for the approach. Next, open the topic Landing.

ld_air.title: Where is the aircraft?
ld_air.text: Is the aircraft in the air?

choices.label: No, it is on the ground

ld_ground.title: On the ground
ld_ground.text: You are on the ground. If you have just landed, open the topic After landing and shutdown.
ld_ground.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER LANDING

ld_before.title: Before landing
ld_before.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), APPROACH and BEFORE LANDING; MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 2 Limitations and section 3 Approach and landing

steps.text: Turn the passenger lights safety button ON.
steps.why: The guide: the safety light plays a safety message over the PA.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), APPROACH item 12 (PASS LIGHTS SAFETY BUTTON ON); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 SAFETY

steps.text: Check the seat belts are adjusted and secure. The BELT button plays the seat belt message over the PA.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), APPROACH item 11 (SEAT BELTS ADJUSTED/SECURE); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 BELT

steps.text: Turn the landing lights ON.
steps.why: If you use the pulse lights, they must be off for night ground operations and for night flight below 300 ft AGL (guide).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), APPROACH item 6 (EXTERIOR LIGHTS AS REQUIRED); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 LNDG (below 10,000 ft by day or night)

steps.text: Check the cabin pressure difference is below 0.5 psi before landing.
steps.why: A checklist item. The sources do not say where to read it.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), APPROACH item 13 (PRESSURIZATION < 0.5 PSI BEFORE LANDING)

steps.text: Lower the landing gear and check three green lights.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE LANDING item 1 (LANDING GEAR DOWN, 3 GREEN)

steps.text: Set the flaps to 35.
steps.warn: Maximum speed with flaps 35 is 160 KIAS.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE LANDING item 2 (FLAPS 35); MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 2 (VFE with flaps 35 degrees: 160 KIAS); sim file asobo-aircraft-cj4, flight_model.cfg, flaps-position.2 = 35 (handle index 2)

steps.text: Check the speed brakes are at 0 %.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE LANDING item 3

steps.text: Fly the approach speed (VAPP) shown on the PFD, with the wind correction if you set one.
steps.why: The community checklist says 'airspeed VREF' at this point. The Operator's Guide recommends VAPP at the final approach fix for a precision approach.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff and landing V-speeds (add half the headwind plus gust, maximum 15 knots)

ld_land.title: Landing
