ld_land.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing (p. 3-5); Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE LANDING and LANDING; MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 2 Limitations

steps.text: Disconnect the autopilot no lower than 200 ft above the ground and turn the yaw damper off before touchdown.
steps.why: The AP button and the YD button toggle. You can also use the autopilot disconnect button on the yoke.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 Autopilot operation limitations and section 3 Approach and landing; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE LANDING item 5

steps.text: Over the runway threshold, pull the thrust levers smoothly back to idle and flare.
steps.why: In this app's catalog the lever event goes to idle with a value of 10 or less.
steps.warn: Limits: tailwind 10 knots, demonstrated crosswind 25 knots, landing weight 15,660 lb.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing (when crossing the runway threshold, pull the power smoothly back to idle and initiate flare and landing); Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), LANDING item 1

steps.text: Touch down on the runway.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing

steps.text: After the nose wheel touches down, apply the brakes.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), LANDING item 2 (BRAKES (AFTER NLG TOUCH) APPLY)

steps.text: Extend the ground spoilers.
steps.why: The CJ4 has no thrust reversers.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing (upon landing, deploy the spoilers and use brakes as needed); Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), LANDING item 3

ld_done.title: Landed
ld_done.text: The aircraft is on the ground. Next, open the topic After landing and shutdown.

sd_ground.title: Where is the aircraft?
sd_ground.text: Is the aircraft on the ground?

sd_air.title: Still flying
sd_air.text: The shutdown is for the ground. Open the topics Descent and approach and Landing first.
sd_air.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER LANDING and SHUTDOWN

sd_after.title: After landing
sd_after.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER LANDING; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 Exterior lights

steps.text: Retract the speed brakes to 0 %.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER LANDING item 1

steps.text: Set the flaps to 0.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER LANDING item 2

steps.text: Turn the pitot/static heat OFF.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER LANDING item 3

steps.text: Turn the ice protection systems OFF, or leave them on if you still need them.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER LANDING item 4 (OFF/AS REQUIRED)

steps.text: Turn the strobe lights off once you are off the runway.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 STROBE (left on until exiting the runway after landing); Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER LANDING item 6

steps.text: Turn the landing lights off and use the taxi light as required.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER LANDING item 6 (EXTERIOR LIGHTS AS REQUIRED); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 TAXI and LNDG

steps.text: Taxi to the parking position.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), SHUTDOWN follows AFTER LANDING

sd_park.title: Shutdown
sd_park.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), SHUTDOWN; CJ4_Checklist.xml

steps.text: Set the parking brake.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), SHUTDOWN item 1 (SET/WHEELS CHOCKED); CJ4_Checklist.xml: Parking_Brake_Set

steps.text: Put the emergency lights switch OFF.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), SHUTDOWN item 2

steps.text: Turn the standby flight display switch OFF.
steps.why: No catalog control exists for this switch.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), SHUTDOWN item 3

steps.text: Set the avionics switch to OFF.
steps.why: Mind the order of the checklist: the avionics go off before the engines are stopped.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), SHUTDOWN item 4

steps.text: Set the climate control selector to OFF.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), SHUTDOWN item 5

steps.text: Turn all the ice protection systems OFF.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), SHUTDOWN item 6 (ICE PROTECTION SYSTEMS (ALL) OFF)

steps.text: Put both thrust levers at IDLE.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), SHUTDOWN item 7; CJ4_Checklist.xml: POWER_LEVERS_IDLE_2ENGINES

steps.text: Press both engine RUN/STOP buttons to STOP.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), SHUTDOWN item 8

check.code: (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:2, Bool) +

steps.text: Turn all the exterior lights OFF.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), SHUTDOWN item 9

check.code: (A:LIGHT BEACON, Bool) (A:LIGHT NAV, Bool) + (A:LIGHT STROBE, Bool) + (A:LIGHT TAXI, Bool) + (A:LIGHT LANDING, Bool) +

steps.text: Turn the battery switch OFF.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), SHUTDOWN item 10

sd_done.title: Shut down
sd_done.text: The engines are stopped and the electrical power is off. The checklist also lists the control lock and the engine covers after the engines have cooled; the simulator has no controls for them.

fe_which.title: What do you want to change?
fe_which.text: What do you want to do?
fe_which.help: These steps use the pilot's CDU. LSK means line select key: L1 is the top key on the left of the CDU screen and R6 the bottom key on the right.

choices.label: Change the destination, arrival or approach

fe_dir.title: Direct to a waypoint
fe_dir.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DIRECT TO; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, classes DirectToPage and DirectToPageController

steps.text: Press the DIR key.
steps.why: This opens the ACT DIRECT-TO page, with the waypoints of your flight plan.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FROM DIR PAGE

steps.text: Press the left key next to the waypoint you want. Use NEXT and PREV for more waypoints.
steps.why: To go to a waypoint that is not in the plan, type its name and press LSK L1 (the line with the arrow) instead.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FROM DIR PAGE; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class DirectToPageController.leftPressed

steps.text: The LEGS page opens with the change marked MOD. Check the first leg, then press EXEC.
steps.why: You cannot go direct to a (VECT) leg. On the LEGS page you can also copy a waypoint to the scratchpad with its left key and then press LSK L2, the TO line (guide).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FROM DIR PAGE (MOD LEGS becomes ACT LEGS); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WT21Fms.onExecButtonPressed and planInMod (sets L:FMC_EXEC_ACTIVE to 1 while a change waits)

fe_near.title: Nearest airport
fe_near.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, classes NearestAirportsPage and NearestAirportsPageController; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 NEAREST AIRPORTS

steps.text: Press the DIR key.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class DirectToPageController.lskR1Pressed; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 NEAREST AIRPORTS

steps.text: Press LSK R1 (NEAREST APTS>).
steps.why: The page lists your origin and destination, then the nearest airports within 200 NM that have a runway of at least 1,500 ft, up to 5 airports. Each line shows the bearing and distance, the fuel you would have on arrival and the time to get there. The guide's editable minimum runway length (default 5,000 ft) is not available in this sim's FMS: MIN RWY is fixed at 1,500 ft.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class DirectToPageController.lskR1Pressed; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 NEAREST AIRPORTS

steps.text: Press the left key next to the airport to go direct to it. The right key (RWxx>) goes direct to that runway with a visual approach.
steps.why: LSK R6 (AIRPORTS>) refreshes the list.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class NearestAirportsPage.select (createDirectToAirport / createDirectToRunwayVisualApproach)

steps.text: The LEGS page opens as MOD. Check it, then press EXEC.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class NearestAirportsPage.select (navigates to the LEGS page); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WT21Fms.onExecButtonPressed and planInMod (sets L:FMC_EXEC_ACTIVE to 1 while a change waits)

fe_hold.title: Fly a hold
fe_hold.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 HOLDS; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, classes HoldListPage, LegsPage (hold selection), FplnHoldPage

steps.text: Press IDX.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class IndexPage (HOLD> on page 1, line 3 right)

steps.text: Press LSK R3 (HOLD>).
steps.why: HOLD> opens the ACT HOLD LIST.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class IndexPage (HOLD> on page 1, line 3 right)

steps.text: Press LSK R6 (NEW HOLD>).
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class HoldListPage.renderHoldRows and onHandleSelectKey

steps.text: On the LEGS page, press the left key next to the fix where you want to hold. For a hold at your position, press LSK R6 (PPOS>).
steps.why: The footer of the page reads HOLD AT. The MOD FPLN HOLD page opens.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class LegsPageController (hold selection) and LegsPage.render (PPOS>)

steps.text: Enter the inbound course and turn direction on the INBD CRS/DIR line, for example 308/R.
steps.why: The ENTRY (direct, teardrop or parallel) is chosen by the FMS from your approach course and cannot be changed.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 CREATING A HOLD (only a 3-digit course and L or R is accepted)

steps.text: Enter either the leg time (minutes) or the leg distance (NM), not both.
steps.why: For example 1.0 minute is about 2.3 NM, and 4.0 NM is about 2.0 minutes (guide). HOLD SPD FAA or ICAO shows the maximum recommended holding speed for your altitude. EFC TIME is advice only.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 CREATING A HOLD (defining one defines the other from the ground speed)

steps.text: Press EXEC.
steps.why: At most six holds can be in the plan (guide); the CDU says TOO MANY HOLDS after that.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 CREATING A HOLD (the fix is duplicated on LEGS and HOLD AT appears above it); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WT21Fms.onExecButtonPressed and planInMod (sets L:FMC_EXEC_ACTIVE to 1 while a change waits)

steps.text: To leave the hold, press LEGS then LSK L6 (<EXIT HOLD). To stay in the hold, press it again (<CANCEL EXIT).
steps.why: If you are already past the hold fix when you arm the exit, the aircraft may leave at once. From elsewhere in the pattern the FMS turns you to the inbound leg and that turn cannot be cancelled (guide).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 EXITING THE HOLD; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class LegsPage.render (<EXIT HOLD / <CANCEL EXIT)

steps.text: To delete a hold, press CLR, then the left key of the hold, then EXEC.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DELETING A HOLD

fe_arr.title: Change destination, arrival or approach
fe_arr.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN, ARRIVAL; MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing

steps.text: To change the destination, press FPLN, type the new airport and press LSK R1 (DEST).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN (DEST can be modified at any time)

steps.text: Press DEP ARR.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 ARRIVAL; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class DepArrPage

steps.text: If the DEP/ARR INDEX shows, press LSK R2 (ARR>).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 ARRIVAL; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class DepArrPage

steps.text: Choose the new STAR, approach or runway.
steps.why: Changing a procedure that you are already flying can cause FMS errors and, in LNAV, send you back to the initial approach fix (guide). Choose the new one early.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 ARRIVAL; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class DepArrPage

steps.text: Press EXEC.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEPART (MOD until EXEC)

steps.text: Check the LEGS page.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEPART (MOD until EXEC)

steps.text: Open APPROACH REF again (PERF, then APPROACH>) and send the speeds again.
steps.why: The landing speeds and distances belong to the runway you chose.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 APPROACH (RWY ID is the arrival runway chosen in DEP/ARR)

fe_wpt.title: Add or delete a waypoint
fe_wpt.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 ADDING A WAYPOINT, DELETING A WAYPOINT, PILOT WAYPOINTS

steps.text: To add a waypoint, press LEGS, type the waypoint and press the left key where it should be inserted.
steps.why: It can be a fix, VOR, NDB, airport or custom waypoint.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 ADDING A WAYPOINT

steps.text: To delete one, press CLR (DELETE shows), then the left key of the waypoint, then EXEC.
steps.why: Some gaps cannot be deleted: after a (VECT) leg, at the end of an airway when the next waypoint is not on it, and before a leg without a defined start such as a DME arc. The CDU says INVALID DELETE when it refuses.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DELETING A WAYPOINT

steps.text: A custom waypoint is typed on the LEGS page as latitude/longitude, as fix/bearing/distance, or as an offset along the track.
steps.why: Examples: N4412.55W00405.25 or N44W00405; OCN090/15/WP1 (15 NM from OCN on bearing 090, named WP1); PADRZ/-10 is 10 NM before PADRZ along the route and PADRZ/10 is 10 NM after it. Custom waypoints are not accepted on the FPLN page. They are stored in the PILOT WPT LIST (IDX, NEXT, DATA BASE>): at most 20, the oldest is replaced by the 21st.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 PILOT WAYPOINTS

fe_altn.title: Alternate airport
fe_altn.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FplnPage and FplnPageController.altnField

steps.text: Press FPLN, type the alternate airport code and press LSK R2 (ALTN).
steps.why: The guide for the older FMS lists ALTN as not implemented; this sim's FMS accepts it.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FplnPageController.altnField (R2; FACILITY NOT FOUND if the airport is unknown)

steps.text: If the page title shows MOD, press EXEC.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEPART (MOD until EXEC)

ap_menu.title: Autopilot
ap_menu.text: What do you want the autopilot to do?
ap_menu.help: The buttons of the flight guidance panel (FGP) toggle: pressing a mode that is on turns it off. Look at the scoreboard at the top of the PFD to see what is on.

choices.label: Turn the autopilot, yaw damper or flight director on or off
Follow the FMS flight plan or a VOR / localizer
Bank limit, speed and Mach, back course

ap_onoff.title: AP, YD and FD
ap_onoff.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 Autopilot operation limitations, FD, YD, AP, YD/AP DISC

steps.text: Press FD to show the flight director bars.
steps.warn: The button toggles. If the bars are already shown, leave it.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 FD (the flight director now gives lateral guidance even with the autopilot off)

steps.text: Press AP to engage the autopilot.
steps.why: Not below 300 ft above the ground after take-off or go-around. The yaw damper is always engaged when the autopilot is.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 AP (engaging the autopilot at once commands the aircraft to follow the selected modes)

steps.text: Press YD to use the yaw damper without the autopilot.
steps.why: The yaw damper must be on after lift-off and off before touchdown.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 YD (YD appears in place of AP on the scoreboard when the yaw damper is on alone)

steps.text: To disconnect, press AP again, or use the yoke disconnect button.
steps.why: Disconnect at 200 ft above the ground at the latest on an approach. The YD/AP DISC breaker bar is for emergencies only, when the autopilot cannot be disconnected normally. Pressing the bar back in reconnects it.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 AP and YD/AP DISC

ap_hdg.title: Heading mode
ap_hdg.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 HDG

steps.text: Turn the HDG knob to the heading you want.
steps.why: Each click moves the heading bug by 1 degree (catalog).
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 HDG

steps.text: Pressing the HDG knob sets the bug to the present heading.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 HDG

steps.text: Press HDG.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 HDG (enables heading hold)

ap_nav.title: NAV mode
ap_nav.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 NAV and section 7 DCP NAV

steps.text: Choose the navigation source with the NAV button on the display control panel above the PFD.
steps.why: FMS1 means the flight plan. VOR1/LOC1 and VOR2/LOC2 are the NAV radios. The preset source can be changed with the DATA knob.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 7 DCP NAV (swaps the active source with the preset: FMS1, VOR1/LOC1, VOR2/LOC2)

steps.text: For a VOR or localizer, set the course with the CRS knob. Pressing the CRS knob gives a course straight to the tuned station.
steps.why: Each click changes the course by 1 degree (catalog).
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 NAV (CRS1 for NAV1, CRS2 for NAV2)

steps.text: Press NAV.
steps.why: On the scoreboard LNV1 is the FMS course; NAV is a VOR or localizer. In this app's tests, pressing NAV with no navigation source engaged nothing.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 NAV (with the FMS as the source it arms LNV and the plane follows the flight plan once within capture distance)

ap_alt.title: Altitude hold
ap_alt.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 ALT

steps.text: Turn the ALT knob to the altitude you want.
steps.why: Each click is 100 ft (catalog). Pressing the knob sets the selected altitude to the present altitude (guide).
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 ALT

steps.text: Press ALT.
steps.why: ALTS CAP on the scoreboard means the selected altitude will be captured; ALT means it is captured (guide).
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 ALT (holds the selected altitude)

ap_vert.title: Vertical mode
ap_vert.text: How should it climb or descend?

choices.label: VNAV: follow the flight plan altitudes

ap_flc.title: Flight level change
ap_flc.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 FLC

steps.text: Set the target altitude with the ALT knob.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 ALT

steps.text: Press FLC.
steps.why: The plane pitches up to slow down and down to speed up. It does not move the thrust levers: the CJ4 has no autothrottle.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 FLC

steps.text: Set the speed with the SPEED knob.
steps.why: Each click is 1 knot (catalog). Pressing the SPEED knob switches between IAS and Mach. The selected speed marker shows on the PFD only while FLC is the active vertical mode.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 FLC

steps.text: Set the thrust yourself for the climb or descent rate you want.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 FLC note

ap_vs.title: Vertical speed
ap_vs.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 VS

steps.text: Set the target altitude with the ALT knob.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 ALT

steps.text: Press VS.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 VS (the plane adjusts pitch to meet the selected vertical speed)

steps.text: Set the rate with the VS wheel.
steps.why: Each click changes the selected rate by 100 fpm, only while VS is engaged (catalog).
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 VS (UP and DOWN on the wheel)

ap_vnav.title: VNAV
ap_vnav.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 VNAV, VNAV operation, VNAV climb, VNAV descent, VNAV path; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 1 Other known issues

steps.text: Make sure the flight plan has the altitude restrictions (LEGS page).
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 VNAV operation (restrictions load with the SID, STAR or approach, or you type them)

steps.text: Press VNAV.
steps.why: In a climb, VNAV does not compute a path: you choose VS or FLC (shown as VVS or VFLC) and VNAV holds an altitude at the climb restrictions. AT OR ABOVE restrictions are up to you. In a descent, PATH is the default mode and follows a computed path at 3 degrees (settable on the VNAV SETUP page), with level-offs at restrictions. VNAV decides climb or descent from the flight plan segment.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 VNAV

steps.text: In a descent, watch for PATH on the scoreboard and the TOD alert on the PFD.
steps.why: PATH arms when you are within 1,000 ft of the path. If the PATH message says it cannot be captured from above, descend to it with VS or FLC. VNAV never moves the thrust levers.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 VNAV PATH and VNAV display

steps.text: If VNAV does not behave as expected, turn it off and on again.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 1 Other known issues

ap_appr.title: Approach mode
ap_appr.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 APPR

steps.text: Set up the approach first (ILS frequency on NAV1 or the approach in the FMS), then press APPR.
steps.why: ILS: APPR arms the localizer (LOC) and the glideslope (GS) while the present mode continues. RNAV: APPR arms APPR LNV and GP. LOC and GS, or LNV and GP, become active when they are captured. In this app's tests, pressing APPR with no navigation source engaged nothing.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 APPR

ap_other.title: Other buttons
ap_other.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 1/2 BANK, B/C, NAV

steps.text: The BANK button limits the bank angle to half.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 1/2 BANK (normal maximum bank 30 degrees, half bank 15 degrees)

steps.text: The B/C (back course) button is not implemented in the sim.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 B/C (NOT IMPLEMENTED)

steps.text: The SPEED knob press switches FLC between IAS and Mach.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 FLC

ga_air.title: Where is the aircraft?
ga_air.text: Is the aircraft in the air?

choices.label: No, it is on the ground

ga_ground.title: On the ground
ga_ground.text: A go-around is flown in the air. After touchdown, open After landing and shutdown, or the topic Take off for a new departure.
ga_ground.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Missed approach / go-around

ga_type.title: Approach in the FMS
ga_type.text: Is an instrument approach loaded in the FMS?
ga_type.help: The FMS loads the missed approach automatically with an instrument approach (guide).

ga_fms.title: FMS missed approach
ga_fms.text: The FMS missed approach can be activated in three ways: press TOGA when the active waypoint is the runway (RWxx), switch the LEGS sequence from INHIBIT to AUTO, or go direct-to a waypoint of the missed approach. Pressing TOGA in the next step does the first one.
ga_fms.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 MISSED APPROACH and SEQUENCING; MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 5 MISSED APPROACH

ga_steps.title: Go-around
ga_steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Missed approach / go-around (p. 3-8); Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), ALL ENGINE GO-AROUND

steps.text: Press the TOGA button.
steps.why: The flight director is set and locked to the present heading and commands 10 degrees nose up (guide). The community checklist says 7.5 degrees then as required.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Missed approach/go-around step 1; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), ALL ENGINE GO-AROUND item 1

steps.text: Push both thrust levers to TO.
steps.why: In this app's catalog the lever event goes to full power with a value of 11 or more.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Missed approach/go-around step 2; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), item 2

steps.text: Set the flaps to 15.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Missed approach/go-around step 3; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), item 4

steps.text: At a positive rate of climb, raise the landing gear.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Missed approach/go-around step 4; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), item 5

steps.text: Press FLC and set 200 knots with the SPEED knob.
steps.why: The speed is your choice; the guide sees no reason to go faster than 200.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Missed approach/go-around step 5

steps.text: At VAPP + 10 knots, set the flaps to 0.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Missed approach/go-around step 6

steps.text: Select the FMS as the navigation source again with the NAV button on the display control panel, then press NAV on the flight guidance panel.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Missed approach/go-around steps 7 and 8 (procedure subject to future changes)

steps.text: Set the thrust as necessary, and turn the yaw damper on.
steps.warn: The earliest height for the yaw damper or autopilot after a go-around is 300 ft above the ground.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Missed approach/go-around step 9; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), items 8 and 9

steps.text: Engage the autopilot as desired.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), ALL ENGINE GO-AROUND item 10

ga_done.title: Climbing away
ga_done.text: Fly the missed approach, then open Descent and approach for another approach, or choose a diversion with the DIR key (Change the flight plan in flight).

li_menu.title: What do you need?
li_menu.text: What do you want to set?

li_lights.title: Exterior lights
li_lights.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 Lighting panel, Exterior lights

steps.text: Beacon: ON before the engine start.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 BEACON

steps.text: Navigation lights: typically left on at all times.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 NAV (red on the left wing tip, green on the right, and a white rear light on each tip)

steps.text: Strobe lights: on when entering an active runway for crossing or for take-off, off after leaving the runway after landing.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 STROBE

steps.text: Taxi light: the normal intensity of the forward-facing lights under the aircraft.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 TAXI

steps.text: Landing lights: the highest intensity of the same lights. Most used for take-off, landing and below 10,000 ft.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 LNDG

steps.text: Logo lights: generally used at night from engine start to engine shutdown.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 LOGO

steps.text: Pulse lights pulse the landing lights and override their steady light.
steps.why: No catalog control exists for the pulse light switch.
steps.warn: The pulse light system must be OFF for all night ground operations and for night flight below 300 ft AGL.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 PULSE LIGHTS

li_ice.title: Ice protection
li_ice.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAXI, BEFORE TAKEOFF, AFTER LANDING, SHUTDOWN; MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 2 Speed limits; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TAKEOFF page 2/3

steps.text: Turn the pitot/static heat ON before take-off and OFF after landing.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAKEOFF item 13 and AFTER LANDING item 3

steps.text: Use the engine anti-ice as required.
steps.why: The sources give no temperature or icing criteria. The minimum speed for sustained icing conditions is 160 KIAS (guide).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAXI item 9 (ENGINE ONLY ANTI-ICE AS REQUIRED)

steps.text: Use the airframe de-ice as required.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), AFTER TAKEOFF item 6 (ICE PROTECTION SYSTEMS AS REQUIRED)

steps.text: Set A/I to ON on the TAKEOFF REF or APPROACH REF page when you use anti-ice.
steps.why: A/I ON slightly lengthens the take-off or landing distance. The CJ4 does not model degraded engine performance with anti-ice on (guide).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TAKEOFF and APPROACH page 2/3 (A/I)

fu_check.title: Fuel on the FMS
fu_check.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 PERF MENU and PERF INIT; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FuelMgmtPage

steps.text: Press the PERF key.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class PerfMenuPage (FUEL MGMT> on line 1 right)

steps.text: Press LSK R1 (FUEL MGMT>).
steps.why: LSK means line select key: R1 is the top key on the right of the CDU screen.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class PerfMenuPage (FUEL MGMT> on line 1 right)

steps.text: Read FUEL, FUEL FLOW, TIME TO RESV and RNG TO RESV.
steps.why: Page 1 also shows SP RNG, GND SPD and RESERVES. Page 2 shows the flow and the fuel used for each engine and the total. Page 3 is the PERF TRIP page with FROM, TO, DIST, GND SPD, ETE and FUEL REQ.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 PERF MENU (FUEL MGMT: current fuel, range, time to reserve and fuel flow)

steps.text: To change the reserve fuel, type a value and press LSK L3 (RESERVES). CLR then L3 puts the default back.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FuelMgmtPage (reserveFuelInput; onDelete resets to the default)

steps.text: Read SENSED FUEL on the PERF INIT page for the fuel on board.
steps.why: The maximum fuel capacity is 5,762 lb (guide, weight and balance).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 PERF INIT (SENSED FUEL: if the amount is changed, re-open the page to refresh it)

ts_menu.title: What is the problem?
ts_menu.help: Each branch asks a few questions. Where the simulator can tell, the answer is filled in for you.

choices.label: An engine will not start or will not keep running
No power, or the displays are dark
The autopilot will not engage, or a mode does nothing
The FMS (CDU) rejects an entry or the plan looks wrong
The aircraft will not accelerate or take off
A switch, key or lever does not respond
A display shows the wrong thing or something is missing

ts_eng_batt.title: Battery
ts_eng_batt.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: Battery_Switch_On_CJ4; MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Engine start (once the BATTERY is on, no other configuration is needed)

steps.text: Turn the battery switch ON.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: Battery_Switch_On_CJ4

ts_eng_q2.title: Power levers
ts_eng_q2.text: Are both power levers at IDLE?

auto.code: (A:GENERAL ENG THROTTLE LEVER POSITION:1, percent) (A:GENERAL ENG THROTTLE LEVER POSITION:2, percent) +

ts_eng_idle.title: Power levers
ts_eng_idle.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: POWER_LEVERS_IDLE_2ENGINES (power levers at IDLE before the start)

steps.text: Put both power levers at IDLE.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: POWER_LEVERS_IDLE_2ENGINES

check.code: (A:GENERAL ENG THROTTLE LEVER POSITION:1, percent) (A:GENERAL ENG THROTTLE LEVER POSITION:2, percent) +

ts_eng_q3.title: Fuel
ts_eng_q3.help: General airmanship: an engine cannot run without fuel. The fuel is also shown on the FMS (PERF, FUEL MGMT>) and as SENSED FUEL on PERF INIT.

ts_eng_nofuel.title: No fuel
ts_eng_nofuel.text: The engines need fuel. The fuel quantity is set outside the cockpit, in the simulator's fuel and payload settings; this guide has no sourced procedure for loading it. After fueling, re-open PERF INIT on the FMS to refresh SENSED FUEL.
ts_eng_nofuel.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 PERF INIT (SENSED FUEL: if the amount is changed, re-access the page to refresh it)

ts_eng_q4.title: Symptom
ts_eng_q4.text: What happens when you try to start?

choices.label: The starter does nothing: N2 does not rise
N2 rises but the engine does not light
It starts, then stops by itself

ts_eng_nospin.title: N2 does not rise
ts_eng_nospin.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Engine start; CJ4_Checklist.xml: RIGHT_ENGINE_STARTER_ON, LEFT_ENGINE_START_REPEAT_PROCEDURE_JET

steps.text: Press the engine starter button once and watch the engine display on the MFD.
steps.why: The sim's checklist starts the right engine first. In the catalog tests the starter raised N2 by about 3 % every 0.7 seconds and dropped out by itself at about 50 % N2. If the battery is on, the levers are at idle and N2 still does not rise, this guide has no further sourced cause.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Engine start (monitor the MFD: STARTER indication, then N2 rises, followed slowly by N1)

ts_eng_nolight.title: N2 rises but no light-off
ts_eng_nolight.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Engine start; CJ4_Checklist.xml: RIGHT_ENG_RUN_BUTTON_RUN_WHEN_N2_20

steps.text: When N2 is at 20 % or more, press the RUN / STOP button of that engine so that it shows RUN.
steps.why: The guide says to press it right after the starter; in the catalog tests the engine lit only when RUN was set with N2 at 20 % or more, which is what the sim's own checklist does. IGN (ignition) shows next to the ITT indicator at 12 % N2.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: RIGHT_ENG_RUN_BUTTON_RUN_WHEN_N2_20; MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Engine start (the STOP indication under the button guard disappears when the starter is pressed and RUN shows once the button is pressed)

steps.text: Watch N1 and ITT rise and settle.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Engine start (N1 and ITT rise before stabilizing at about 25 % N1 and 600 degrees C ITT, then IGN goes out)

check.code: (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:2, Bool) +

ts_eng_stops.title: The engine stops by itself
ts_eng_stops.text: If an engine does not start or shuts off at random, a mixture axis bound to your hardware can be the cause: check your controller bindings and remove any mixture axis. Also check that the RUN / STOP button of the engine still shows RUN (the catalog says setting it to 0 stops the engine and it reads 1 while the engine runs).
ts_eng_stops.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 1 Common fixes (Engines not starting/shutting off randomly: rogue mixture axis bound to hardware, check hardware binds); written for the community mod

ts_pwr_batt.title: Battery
ts_pwr_batt.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 BATTERY

steps.text: Turn the battery switch ON.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 BATTERY (the battery master switch supplies main electrical power to the aircraft)

ts_pwr_q2.title: Avionics switch
ts_pwr_q2.help: The switch has three positions (catalog: 1 = OFF, 0 = ON, 2 = DISPATCH). The sim's checklist uses DISPATCH for the start and ON after it.

ts_pwr_disp.title: DISPATCH mode
ts_pwr_disp.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 AVIONICS and DISPATCH; CJ4_Checklist.xml: Avionics_Bus_Switch_On

steps.text: Set the avionics switch to ON.
steps.why: In DISPATCH the PFDs and the right-hand displays stay dark, and only COM1, NAV1, ATC1 and ADF are available on the TUN page. The sim's checklist sets ON after the engine start.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 AVIONICS (in DISPATCH only the left MFD and the left FMS are active; ON powers all avionics)

ts_pwr_avi.title: Avionics switch OFF
ts_pwr_avi.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 AVIONICS; CJ4_Checklist.xml: Avionics_Bus_Switch_On

steps.text: Set the avionics switch to DISPATCH or ON.
steps.why: Use DISPATCH if you only want the left MFD and left FMS before the engine start, ON for everything.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 AVIONICS; CJ4_Checklist.xml: Avionics_Bus_Switch_On (DISPATCH value 2, ON value 0)

ts_pwr_gen.title: Generators and brightness
ts_pwr_gen.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 L/R GEN, DIMMING; CJ4_Checklist.xml: GENERATOR_MAIN_2

steps.text: Turn both generator switches ON.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: GENERATOR_MAIN_2; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 L/R GEN

check.code: (A:GENERAL ENG MASTER ALTERNATOR:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG MASTER ALTERNATOR:2, Bool) +

steps.text: Turn the display brightness knobs up on the lighting panel.
steps.why: PFD1 is the left, pilot-side display and PFD2 the right one. The panel dimming knob is separate.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 DIMMING (PFD1/2: outer knob; MFD1/2: inner knob; each side is independent)

steps.text: If you are parked where ground power exists, you can switch it on from the FMS.
steps.why: Only at a designated parking spot that has ground power. This guide has no further sourced cause for a dark cockpit.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class UserSettingsPage (IDX, NEXT, SETTINGS>, GROUND POWER); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 MOD SET (GROUND POWER UNIT)

ts_ap_q1.title: Flight director
ts_ap_q1.help: The mode buttons were verified on a CJ4 with the flight director on (catalog).

ts_ap_fd.title: Flight director
ts_ap_fd.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 FD

steps.text: Press FD to turn the flight director on.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 FD

choices.label: The autopilot or a mode drops out
It works with the mouse but not from my keys or hardware

ts_ap_engage.title: The autopilot will not engage
ts_ap_engage.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 Autopilot operation limitations, AP, YD/AP DISC

steps.text: Check that you are at least 300 ft above the ground after take-off or go-around.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 (minimum engage height after take-off: 300 ft AGL)

steps.text: Check that the YD/AP DISC breaker bar is pushed in.
steps.why: No catalog control exists for the breaker bar.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 YD/AP DISC (the bar disconnects the flight guidance system; pressing it back in reconnects it)

steps.text: Press AP once. It toggles.
steps.why: If you press it twice it disengages again. Look at the scoreboard at the top of the PFD.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 AP; catalog note (every event toggles the autopilot, whatever its value)

ts_ap_mode.title: A mode does nothing
ts_ap_mode.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 NAV, APPR, FLC, VNAV; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 SEQUENCING and section 1 Other known issues

steps.text: NAV and APPR need a navigation source: the FMS with a flight plan, or a tuned VOR or localizer.
steps.why: Choose the source with the NAV button on the display control panel. Tune the radio on the TUN page.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 NAV and APPR; catalog notes (pressed with the flight director on and no navigation source, nothing engaged)

steps.text: A selected-speed marker shows only while FLC is the active vertical mode.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 FLC

steps.text: If the aircraft keeps turning back to the last waypoint, set the LEGS sequence back to AUTO.
steps.why: On the LEGS page the SEQUENCE line (AUTO / INHIBIT) is on line 1 right.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 SEQUENCING (with INHIBIT selected and the autopilot in FMS NAV mode, the aircraft circles back to the last waypoint)

steps.text: If VNAV does not behave as expected, turn it off and on again.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 1 Other known issues

ts_ap_drop.title: A mode drops out
ts_ap_drop.text: Changing the navigation source disables the autopilot modes, so choose the new modes again afterwards. On an ILS the FMS itself switches the source to NAV1 when the localizer is captured. The sources describe no other automatic disconnect.
ts_ap_drop.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class NavToNavTransferred (comment: switching the nav source disables any autopilot modes); MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 APPR

ts_ap_keys.title: Keys and hardware
ts_ap_keys.text: The guide for the community mod says autopilot modes could not be triggered from key bindings or controllers. In this app's catalog, the autopilot, yaw damper, flight director and mode buttons were verified on a real CJ4: each event toggles the function whatever its value, so send it once and nothing on release. The heading, altitude, speed and course knobs take +1 and -1 per click.
ts_ap_keys.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 1 Other known issues; catalog notes of AUTOPILOT_AP_1, AUTOPILOT_Heading_Mode, AUTOPILOT_Altitude

ts_fms_q.title: What do you see?
ts_fms_q.text: What do you see on the CDU?

choices.label: FACILITY NOT FOUND or NOT IN DATABASE
AIRWAY NOT FOUND or INVALID AIRWAY ...
A gap or boxes in the route
My change does not take effect
The ILS is not tuned or APPR does not arm

ts_fms_notfound.title: FACILITY NOT FOUND
ts_fms_notfound.text: The FMS could not find what you typed. Check the spelling: airports use their ICAO code, VORs their 3-letter name, fixes their name (for example CHKNN). If the name is right, press the same key again, or clear the message and type it again: the guide says an airport can be refused on the first press even when it is valid. Custom waypoints must be typed on the LEGS page in the formats latitude/longitude, fix/bearing/distance or fix/distance.
ts_fms_notfound.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN (NOT IN DATABASE note) and PILOT WAYPOINTS; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FplnPageController (throws FACILITY NOT FOUND)

ts_fms_xside.title: XSIDE EDIT IN PROGRESS
ts_fms_xside.text: The other FMS (the copilot's CDU) has a change that is waiting for EXEC, and you cannot edit the plan from this one until it is done. Go to the other CDU and press EXEC, or CANCEL MOD there.
ts_fms_xside.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WT21Fms.canEditPlan (false when the other side's plan is in MOD and this side's is not)

ts_fms_notground.title: NOT ON GROUND
ts_fms_notground.text: The origin airport can only be set on the ground. In the air you can change the destination, the arrival and the approach (topic Change the flight plan in flight).
ts_fms_notground.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN (ORIGIN: cannot be modified once airborne); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FplnPageController.setOrigin

ts_fms_invalid.title: INVALID ENTRY
ts_fms_invalid.text: The page did not accept the format. Accepted formats: wind direction/speed such as 240/6 (direction 0 to 360, speed up to 100); temperature as a whole number of degrees C from -54 to 54; altimeter as 29.92, as 2992, or a 4-digit hPa value below 2000; runway slope up to 2 % with U or D (U1.6, D.5); cruise altitude 0 to 45000 ft or FL; COM frequency 118 to 137 MHz; NAV frequency 108 to 117.95 MHz in 50 kHz steps; transponder code 4 digits from 0 to 7; passengers as a number or number/weight. Restrictions: 250/18000, 18000B, 9000A, and a / first for altitudes below 500.
ts_fms_invalid.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, classes WindFormat, TemperatureFormat, PerfQnhFormat, RwySlopeFormat, AltitudeInputFormat, ComFrequencyFormat, NavFrequencyFormat, TransponderCodeFormat, PassengerDataFormat; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 CONSTRAINTS

ts_fms_airway.title: Airway messages
ts_fms_airway.text: AIRWAY NOT FOUND: the airway does not pass through the waypoint of the row above. INVALID AIRWAY EXIT: the exit waypoint is not on that airway. INVALID LINE SELECTED: press the exit key on the same row as the airway. INVALID AIRWAY LOCATION: airways can only follow the departure or the enroute part of the plan. A STAR or approach that is already loaded can also block airway entries, so enter the airways first.
ts_fms_airway.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FplnPageController.takeAirwayEntry and takeLegEntry; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN

ts_fms_pos.title: Initialize the position
ts_fms_pos.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 POS INIT; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, classes IndexPage and PosInitPage

steps.text: Press IDX.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class IndexPage

steps.text: Press LSK L3 (<POS INIT).
steps.why: LSK means line select key: L3 is the third key down on the left of the CDU screen.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class IndexPage

steps.text: Press LSK R4 (SET POS TO GNSS).
steps.why: The line then reads COMPLETE and the message goes away.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 POS INIT (press LSK 4R); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class PosInitPage

ts_fms_disco.title: A gap in the route
ts_fms_disco.text: A gap (boxes on the LEGS or FPLN page) is a break in the route, for example between a STAR and an approach. Delete it with CLR, then the left key next to it, then EXEC; or type the next waypoint over it. It cannot be deleted after a (VECT) leg (drop the next waypoint onto the (VECT) or delete the (VECT)), at the end of an airway when the next waypoint is not on that airway, or before a leg without a defined start such as a DME arc. A (VECT) leg means radar vectors: use HDG mode and follow ATC.
ts_fms_disco.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 OTHER WAYPOINTS, DISCONTINUITY, DELETING A WAYPOINT

ts_fms_mod.title: Changes do not take effect
ts_fms_mod.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEPART (MOD until EXEC), SEQUENCING; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WT21Fms.onExecButtonPressed

steps.text: Look for MOD in the page title. If it shows, press EXEC.
steps.why: A change stays in a modified copy of the plan until EXEC. To drop it, use <CANCEL MOD (LSK L6).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEPART (MOD in the top left corner until EXEC has been pressed); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WT21Fms.onExecButtonPressed

steps.text: If the CDU says XSIDE EDIT IN PROGRESS, finish or cancel the change on the other CDU.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WT21Fms.canEditPlan

steps.text: On the LEGS page, check that SEQUENCE is on AUTO (line 1 right).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 SEQUENCING (INHIBIT stops the FMS moving on to the next waypoint)

ts_fms_perf.title: No V-speeds or performance data
ts_fms_perf.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff and landing V-speeds; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 PERF INIT, TAKEOFF, APPROACH; MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 7 REFS

steps.text: Choose the runway in DEP ARR first: the departure runway for TAKEOFF REF, the arrival runway (and approach) for APPROACH REF.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff and landing V-speeds (a departure and arrival runway must be selected through DEP/ARR before using the PERF pages)

steps.text: Enter the weights on PERF INIT.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff and landing V-speeds (the speeds use what the pilot inputs, not the sim weights); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 PERF INIT

steps.text: On the TAKEOFF or APPROACH REF page, fill in OAT and QNH, the two required fields. Wind is optional (blank means calm).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TAKEOFF (OAT and QNH required for the speeds)

steps.text: Press SEND> on page 2 and check the speeds appear on the PFD.
steps.why: If you changed a speed by hand with the REFS MENU, enable it with the check mark before it shows on the speed tape again (guide).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TAKEOFF page 2/3 (IN PROGRESS then COMPLETE)

ts_fms_ils.title: The ILS is not tuned
ts_fms_ils.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WT21NavToNavManager; MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 APPR

steps.text: Make sure the ILS approach is loaded in the plan (DEP ARR, ARR>, approach on the right, EXEC).
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing

steps.text: Make sure the FMS is the navigation source.
steps.why: The FMS tunes the localizer itself when you are within about 31 NM of the destination (TERM). The message LOC WILL BE TUNED shows, and about 30 seconds later NAV1 and NAV2 are on the ILS frequency.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class NavToNavOff (the localizer is tuned only with the FMS as the active source)

steps.text: Open the TUN page and check NAV1. If needed, type the ILS frequency and press LSK L3.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Approach and landing (confirm the proper ILS frequency is set in the TUN page for NAV1)

steps.text: Press APPR to arm the localizer and glideslope.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 APPR; catalog note (pressed with the flight director on and no navigation source, nothing engaged)

ts_fms_sb.title: SimBrief import fails
ts_fms_sb.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, classes UserSettingsPage, RouteMenuPage, FmcFplnRequestSystem; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 1 SIMBRIEF

steps.text: Check the SimBrief pilot ID or user name on the SETTINGS page.
steps.why: IDX, NEXT, then LSK R6 (SETTINGS>), line L3. The pilot ID is the 5 or 6 digit number in the SimBrief dispatch options.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class UserSettingsPage.simbriefUsernameField (INVALID SB USER if the name is not found)

steps.text: Check the internet connection, then try <FPLN RECALL again (IDX, ROUTE MENU>, LSK L3).
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class RouteMenuPage (DL FPLN FAILED when the request fails)

steps.text: Release the parking brake.
steps.source: CJ4_Checklist.xml: Parking_Brake_Release

auto.code: (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:1, Bool) (A:GENERAL ENG COMBUSTION:2, Bool) +

ts_acc_noeng.title: An engine is not running
ts_acc_noeng.text: Start the engines first (topic Start the engines). If an engine stops by itself, see Troubleshooting, An engine will not start or will not keep running.

ts_acc_list.title: Thrust and configuration
ts_acc_list.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure; Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAKEOFF; MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 2 Limitations

steps.text: Push both thrust levers fully forward to the TO detent.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure (advance throttle to TO detent, full forward); the CLB detent gives climb power

steps.text: Check the speed brakes are at 0 %.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Quick Reference Checklist (community PDF), BEFORE TAKEOFF item 5

steps.text: Check the weight against the limit: 17,110 lb at take-off.
steps.why: On TAKEOFF REF page 2, compare TOFL with the runway length. If TOFL is longer than the runway, the aircraft needs more runway than there is.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 2 Weight limits; sim file asobo-aircraft-cj4, panel/Instruments/WT21/Plugins/CJ4FmcPlugins.js, class CJ4TakeoffRefPage (the TOW shows yellow above the maximum)

steps.text: Remember that take-off power is limited to 5 minutes.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 2 Engine limits (maximum sustained TO power: 5 minutes total per engine start/stop cycle)

steps.text: Check your hardware: a stray mixture axis can shut the engines off.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 1 Common fixes

choices.label: A thrust lever does not move or moves by itself
Autopilot buttons from my keys or hardware
A switch from this app does the opposite

ts_ctl_thr.title: Thrust levers
ts_ctl_thr.text: The guide for the community mod lists two causes: a custom livery that brings its own panel.cfg can leave the FADEC (the engine control) inoperative, so the levers do not move although the engines respond; use the default livery or remove the livery's panel.cfg. Also look for a stray SimConnect.cfg in your Documents folder. A mixture axis bound to hardware can shut the engines off.
ts_ctl_thr.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 1 Known issues and Common fixes (written for the community mod)

ts_ctl_toga.title: TOGA button
ts_ctl_toga.text: The Operator's Guide says the throttle TOGA button was not working and suggests binding the AUTO THROTTLE TO GA event to a key or a hardware switch. This sim's cockpit file defines TOGA_PUSH on the throttle button (ENGINE_Button_TOGA_1) and a shortcut on the fire bottle under the L ENG FIRE button, both sending AUTO_THROTTLE_TO_GA, and the FMS intercepts that event to set TO mode.
ts_ctl_toga.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 3 Takeoff procedure NOTE; sim file asobo-aircraft-cj4, model/CJ4_Cockpit.xml (TOGA_PUSH templates); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WT21APStateManager (AUTO_THROTTLE_TO_GA intercepted)

ts_ctl_audio.title: No radio audio
ts_ctl_audio.text: On the audio panel, the button above a COM label chooses the transmit radio (a green light shows it) and the knob below mutes or unmutes it. A knob turned all the way left (COM1) is full volume and a knob pointing straight up is muted; you can mute the radio you transmit on. Check the frequency on the TUN page. In DISPATCH only COM1 works. If COM2 shows CROSS-SIDE TUNING INOPERATIVE in yellow, the second radio has no power.
ts_ctl_audio.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 8 COM 1/2 and DISPATCH; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class TunePage.render (CROSS-SIDE TUNING INOPERATIVE)

ts_ctl_sw.title: Switch states
ts_ctl_sw.text: The catalog notes say: for the battery and the generators, setting 0 is ON and 1 is OFF; the avionics switch is 1 = OFF, 0 = ON, 2 = DISPATCH; lights, pitot heat and anti-ice take 1 for on and 0 for off; the starters take 1 and drop out by themselves at about 50 % N2; RUN / STOP takes 1 (lights the engine only at N2 of 20 % or more) and 0 (stops it); the parking brake takes 100 for set and 0 for release; the flaps axis takes 0, 8192 and 16384 for positions 0, 1 and 2; the spoilers axis runs from 0 to 16384; the thrust lever event goes to idle with 10 or less and to full power with 11 or more; the VS wheel moves 100 fpm per click only in VS mode; the autopilot, yaw damper, flight director and mode buttons toggle on every event whatever the value.
ts_ctl_sw.source: catalog notes (data/asobo_cj4_catalog.json), checked on a running CJ4; CJ4_Checklist.xml: Avionics_Bus_Switch_On

ts_disp_q.title: Which display problem?
ts_disp_q.text: What is wrong with the display?

choices.label: No speeds on the speed tape
The selected speed marker is missing
Altitude or pressure in the wrong unit
The PLAN map does not follow the aircraft

ts_disp_bug.title: Selected speed marker
ts_disp_bug.text: The selected speed marker is not visible on the PFD unless FLC is the active vertical mode. Press FLC to see it.
ts_disp_bug.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 6 FLC

ts_disp_tfc.title: Traffic
ts_disp_tfc.text: On the PFD in ARC or ROSE mode, traffic is only shown with TERR or WX turned on. The TFC button shows or hides traffic. The maximum TCAS display range is 40 NM and resolution advisories are not modelled.
ts_disp_tfc.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 7 TFC and section 5 TCAS CONTROL

ts_disp_units.title: Units
ts_disp_units.text: The PFD pressure unit (inches or hPa) and the altitude in metres are set in the PFD MENU, CONFIG (PRESSURE, MTRS ALT). The guide notes that the FMS/MFD units setting does not change the PFD units.
ts_disp_units.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 7 PFD MENU CONFIG and section 5 MOD SET (FMS/MFD UNITS)

ts_disp_plan.title: PLAN map
ts_disp_plan.text: In PLAN view the map follows the aircraft until you step through a waypoint with the MFD ADV page of the CDU; after that it cannot be re-centered on the aircraft. The real unit never centers on the aircraft.
ts_disp_plan.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 7 LWR MENU FORMAT note and section 5 MFD ADV

ts_disp_chart.title: Charts
ts_disp_chart.text: Electronic charts on the MFD need a Navigraph chart subscription linked to the aircraft, and an origin and/or destination in the flight plan.
ts_disp_chart.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 7 ELECTRONIC CHARTS

cdu_menu.title: FMS CDU
cdu_menu.text: Which CDU page or function do you need?
cdu_menu.help: These steps use the pilot's CDU (the left one). The CDU is the FMS keypad and screen. The sources describe the Working Title FMS of the CJ4 (a Collins FMS-3000 look-alike).

choices.label: The letter, digit and symbol keys
Line select keys (the keys beside the screen)
IDX and the pages behind it

cdu_kb.title: Typing on the CDU
cdu_kb.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, classes FmcKeyboardInput, WT21FmcScreen, FmcEventPublisher

steps.text: Type with the keys of the CDU. What you type appears on the last line of the screen, the scratchpad, between brackets.
steps.why: The scratchpad holds your entry until you press a line select key, which puts it into the field next to that key, or until you clear it. Use the topic The letter, digit and symbol keys for the keys.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WT21FmcScreen.SCRATCHPAD_OPTIONS (scratchpad on the last row, surrounded by brackets)

steps.text: Or type on your computer keyboard: click the CDU screen first.
steps.why: Letters, digits, space, / . + and - work. Backspace works like CLR, Ctrl+Backspace clears the whole scratchpad, and the left and right arrow keys work as PREV and NEXT. The mode switches itself off after 30 seconds without a key, or when you click again.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FmcKeyboardInput (click on the screen toggles keyboard input; KB INPUT ACTIVE message; scratchpad brackets blink)

steps.text: If the page does not accept what you typed, the scratchpad shows a message such as INVALID ENTRY or FACILITY NOT FOUND.
steps.why: See the topic Troubleshooting, FMS, for what each message means.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, classes FplnPageController and WT21FmcScreen.SCRATCHPAD_OPTIONS (clearScratchpadOnError); msfssdk.js (textInputFieldParseFailThrowValue: INVALID ENTRY)

cdu_alnum.title: Letter, digit and symbol keys
cdu_alnum.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FmcEventPublisher.dispatchHEvent and WT21FmcScreen (scratchpad_plus_minus)

steps.text: Letter keys A to Z: each press adds that letter to the scratchpad.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FmcEventPublisher.dispatchHEvent (alpha events add their character)

steps.text: Digit keys 0 to 9: each press adds that digit.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FmcEventPublisher.dispatchHEvent

steps.text: SP adds a space, the dot key adds a point and the slash key adds a /.
steps.why: The slash separates the two parts of an entry such as wind 240/6, passengers 6/180 or a restriction 250/18000.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FmcEventPublisher.dispatchHEvent (SP becomes a space, DOT a point, DIV a slash)

steps.text: The +/- key adds a minus sign. If the entry already ends with - or +, it flips it to the other sign.
steps.why: For a temperature below zero press +/- first, then the digits.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WT21FmcScreen (scratchpad_plus_minus)

cdu_lsk.title: Line select keys
cdu_lsk.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WT21CduDisplay.addLskEvents and PageLinkField; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5

steps.text: The six keys on each side of the screen are the line select keys (LSK): L1 to L6 on the left, R1 to R6 on the right, counted from the top.
steps.why: Each key works on the line next to it.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WT21CduDisplay.addLskEvents (L1 to L6 and R1 to R6 map to the lines 1 to 6 of the screen, left and right)

steps.text: With text in the scratchpad, a line select key puts it into the field on that line, if the field accepts it.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FplnPageController (setOrigin, setDestination and takeLegEntry take the scratchpad contents); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 ADDING A WAYPOINT

steps.text: With an empty scratchpad, many fields copy their value into the scratchpad when you press their key.
steps.why: You can then press another key to use that value somewhere else, for example to copy a waypoint.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FplnPage.originField (empty scratchpad returns the ident); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DIRECT TO (FROM LEGS PAGE)

steps.text: A name with < before it or > after it is a link. Press its key to open that page.
steps.why: Greyed entries are not available in the sim.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class PageLinkField (for example <PERF INIT, FUEL MGMT>, ARR>)

steps.text: A field showing options such as DRY / WET or OFF / ON changes when you press its key.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class CJ4TakeoffRefPage (RWY COND DRY/WET, A/I OFF/ON, T/O FLAPS 0/15)

cdu_page.title: NEXT and PREV page
cdu_page.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, classes LegsPage.onHandleScrolling, DepArrPage.onHandleScrolling, FplnPage.onHandleScrolling; Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5

steps.text: Press NEXT page for the next page of the same function.
steps.why: The page number is shown at the top right of the screen, for example 1/3. On the LEGS and DEP ARR pages NEXT after the last page returns to page 1.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class LegsPage.onHandleScrolling (pageRight)

steps.text: Press PREV page to go back one page.
steps.why: PREV on page 1 of the LEGS or DEP ARR pages goes to the last page.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class LegsPage.onHandleScrolling (pageLeft)

cdu_exec.title: EXEC and MOD
cdu_exec.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEPART and FPLN; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WT21Fms.onExecButtonPressed

steps.text: While a change waits, the page title shows MOD. Press EXEC to make it active.
steps.why: Nothing is changed in the aircraft until EXEC. EXEC also saves the plan into the simulator's own flight plan; the guide warns this sync does not always match the FMS plan.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEPART (MOD appears in the top left corner until EXEC has been pressed); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WT21Fms.onExecButtonPressed (copies the modified plan to the active plan)

steps.text: To drop a waiting change, press <CANCEL MOD (LSK L6).
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, classes FplnPage, LegsPage, PerfInitPage and DepArrPageController.onLskL6 (cancel the MOD)

cdu_clr.title: CLR / DEL
cdu_clr.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WT21FmcScreen (clear_del, clear_del_long); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DELETING A WAYPOINT

steps.text: With text in the scratchpad, CLR deletes the last character. Holding CLR clears the whole scratchpad.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WT21FmcScreen (clear_del: backspace; clear_del_long: clear)

steps.text: With an empty scratchpad, CLR puts DELETE in the scratchpad. Then press the line select key of the entry to delete.
steps.why: This deletes a waypoint, a hold, a restriction or resets a field. If the field cannot be deleted the CDU says INVALID DELETE.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class WT21FmcScreen (clear_del with empty scratchpad starts the delete mode); Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DELETING A WAYPOINT (CLR DEL, DELETE appears, press the left LSK)

cdu_fpln.title: FPLN page
cdu_fpln.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN (ACT FPLN); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FplnPage

steps.text: Press FPLN to open the flight plan: ACT FPLN, or MOD FPLN while a change waits.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FplnPageController.activeHeaderString and modHeaderString

steps.text: ORIGIN (LSK L1) and DEST (LSK R1) take the 3 or 4 letter airport code. DIST shows the direct distance between them.
steps.why: A new origin on the ground clears the plan; the origin cannot be changed in flight. The destination can be changed at any time.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN (ORIGIN, DIST, DEST)

steps.text: ALTN (LSK R2) takes an alternate airport. ORIG RWY shows the departure runway chosen on DEP ARR.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FplnPage.renderMainPage and FplnPageController.altnField

steps.text: VIA and TO (line 4) show the first leg: the SID and its exit, or DIRECT and the first waypoint. Type a waypoint and press LSK R4 to set it.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN (VIA, TO)

steps.text: FLT NO (LSK R5) takes a flight number of up to 8 characters.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FplnPage.fltNoField (maxLength 8)

steps.text: PERF INIT> (LSK R6) opens PERF INIT. <CANCEL MOD (LSK L6) drops a waiting change.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FplnPage.renderMainPage

steps.text: NEXT page shows the route pages: five VIA / TO rows per page. Airways go in VIA (left keys) and waypoints in TO (right keys).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FPLN (VIA / TO from page 2); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class FplnPageController (five rows per page)

cdu_legs.title: LEGS page
cdu_legs.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 LEGS, CONSTRAINTS, SEQUENCING, LABEL LINES, OTHER WAYPOINTS; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class LegsPage

steps.text: Press LEGS to see every waypoint of the plan on the left and its speed / altitude restriction on the right.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 LEGS

steps.text: Above each waypoint the track and the distance from the previous waypoint are shown.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 LABEL LINES

steps.text: Line 1 is the FROM waypoint and line 2 the TO waypoint, the one you are flying to. On the FROM line, LSK R1 switches SEQUENCE between AUTO and INHIBIT.
steps.why: In AUTO the FMS moves on to the next waypoint after passing one. In INHIBIT it does not. At the end of the plan, at the runway, the FMS goes to INHIBIT by itself.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 SEQUENCING; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class LegsPageController (SEQUENCE AUTO / INHIBIT)

steps.text: To add a restriction, type it and press the right key next to the waypoint. A waypoint typed and sent with a left key is inserted there.
steps.why: Formats: 250/18000, 18000B (at or below), 9000A (at or above), FL200. A number below 500 is a speed; type a / first for an altitude below 500.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 CONSTRAINTS and ADDING A WAYPOINT

steps.text: A (VECT) line means radar vectors: use HDG mode. A number in brackets such as (2299) is an altitude restriction without a waypoint.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 OTHER WAYPOINTS

steps.text: <CANCEL MOD (LSK L6) drops a waiting change. When the active leg is a hold, L6 shows <EXIT HOLD.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class LegsPage.render

cdu_deparr.title: DEP ARR
cdu_deparr.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEP ARR, DEP/ARR INDEX, DEPART, ARRIVAL; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class DepArrPage and DepArrPageController

steps.text: Press DEP ARR. It opens the DEP/ARR INDEX, or the ACT ARRIVAL page when you are in flight more than 50 NM from the destination or halfway there.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEP ARR

steps.text: On the index, press LSK L1 (<DEP) for the origin's departures and LSK R2 (ARR>) for the destination's arrivals.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class DepArrPage.getIndexTemplate and onHandleSelectKey

steps.text: DEPART shows DEPARTURES (SIDs) on the left and RUNWAYS on the right. ARRIVAL shows STARS on the left and APPROACHES on the right; visual approaches appear as RW and the runway number.
steps.why: The chosen item turns green and its transitions (TRANS) are listed. Press a green item again to remove it. NEXT and PREV show more pages.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEPART and ARRIVAL; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class DepArrPageController.renderDepArrTemplate

steps.text: Press EXEC to accept. LSK L6 (<DEP/ARR IDX) goes back to the index, or cancels a waiting change (<CANCEL MOD). LSK R6 (LEGS>) opens the LEGS page.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DEPART (MOD until EXEC); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class DepArrPageController.renderDepArrTemplate and onLskL6

cdu_perf.title: PERF
cdu_perf.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 PERF MENU, PERF INIT, TAKEOFF, APPROACH, VNAV SETUP, FUEL MGMT, FLT LOG; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class PerfMenuPage; sim file asobo-aircraft-cj4, panel/Instruments/WT21/Plugins/CJ4FmcPlugins.js, class CJ4PerfMenuPageExtension

steps.text: Press PERF to open the PERF MENU.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 PERF MENU

steps.text: <PERF INIT (LSK L1): weights and cruise altitude.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 PERF INIT

steps.text: <VNAV SETUP (LSK L2): three pages for the VNAV climb (TGT SPEED, TRANS ALT), cruise (TGT SPEED, CRZ ALT) and descent (TGT SPEED, TRANS FL, VPA).
steps.why: VPA is the descent flight path angle; the default is 3 degrees (guide).
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 PERF MENU (VNAV SETUP); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class VNAVSetupPage

steps.text: <TAKEOFF (LSK L3): TAKEOFF REF. APPROACH> (LSK R3): APPROACH REF.
steps.source: sim file asobo-aircraft-cj4, panel/Instruments/WT21/Plugins/CJ4FmcPlugins.js, class CJ4PerfMenuPageExtension (line 3)

steps.text: FUEL MGMT> (LSK R1): fuel, fuel flow, range and time to reserve. FLT LOG> (LSK R2): take-off and landing times, en route time, distances, fuel used and speeds.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 PERF MENU; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, classes FuelMgmtPage, FlightLogPage

steps.text: ADVISORY VNAV (LSK L5) chooses ENABLE or DISABLE.
steps.source: MSFS CJ4 Operator's Guide v1, section 5 PERF MENU (ADVISORY VNAV: advisory VNAV information on the PFD/MFD even when VNAV is not enabled); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class PerfMenuPage.advisoryVnavSwitch

cdu_dir.title: DIR
cdu_dir.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 DIRECT TO, NEAREST AIRPORTS; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, classes DirectToPage and DirectToPageController

steps.text: Press DIR to open ACT DIRECT-TO with the waypoints of the plan.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FROM DIR PAGE

steps.text: Press the left key next to a waypoint to go direct to it. The LEGS page then opens as MOD: press EXEC.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 FROM DIR PAGE; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class DirectToPageController.leftPressed

steps.text: To go to any waypoint, type it and press LSK L1 (the line with the arrow).
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class DirectToPageController.lskL1Pressed

steps.text: NEAREST APTS> (LSK R1) lists the nearest airports.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 NEAREST AIRPORTS

steps.text: ALT SEL (LSK R6) copies the altitude selected on the flight guidance panel into the scratchpad.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class DirectToPageController.lskR6Pressed

cdu_idx.title: IDX
cdu_idx.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class IndexPage

steps.text: Press IDX to open the INDEX. Page 1 has <DATALINK (L1), <STATUS (L2), <POS INIT (L3), FREQUENCY> (R1), FIX> (R2), HOLD> (R3), PROG> (R4) and ROUTE MENU> (R6).
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class IndexPage.render (page 1/2)

steps.text: Page 2 (NEXT page) has DATA BASE> (R1), DEFAULTS> (R3) and SETTINGS> (R6).
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class IndexPage.render (page 2/2)

steps.text: STATUS shows the navigation data base dates, UTC and the date. POS INIT sets the position (LSK R4). HOLD> opens the hold list. ROUTE MENU> holds <FPLN RECALL for SimBrief. SETTINGS> has ground power, cabin lights and the SimBrief ID. DATA BASE> holds the pilot waypoints.
steps.why: Entries shown greyed, such as <MCDU MENU, <VORDME CTL, <GNSS CTL, SEC FPLN>, <FMS CTL, DB DISK OPS> and ARR DATA>, are not available in this sim.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 STATUS, POS INIT, HOLDS, PILOT WAYPOINTS, MOD SET; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, classes StatusPage, PosInitPage, RouteMenuPage, UserSettingsPage, DatabasePage

steps.text: FREQUENCY>, FIX>, PROG>, <DATALINK and DEFAULTS> open further pages. The sources read for this guide do not describe them.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class IndexPage (links)

cdu_tun.title: TUN
cdu_tun.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TUN, ATC CONTROL, TCAS CONTROL; sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class TunePage

steps.text: Press TUN to open the TUNE page.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TUN

steps.text: COM1 (LSK L1) and COM2 (LSK R1) are the active frequencies. RECALL (LSK L2 and R2) holds the other frequency. Press the RECALL key with an empty scratchpad to swap.
steps.source: Working Title CJ4 Operator's Guide 0.12.13, section 5 TUN (COM1, COM2, RECALL); sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class TunePage.com1StandbyField

steps.text: NAV1 (LSK L3) and NAV2 (LSK R3) take a frequency or a 3-letter VOR. The field shows AUTO or MAN.
steps.source: sim file workingtitle-instruments-wt21 2.0.4, wt21/FMC/FMC.js, class TunePage.nav1ActiveField and NavFrequencyFormat

steps.text: ATC1 (LSK L5) is the transponder code. TCAS MODE (LSK R5) chooses TA, RA or STBY. TCAS> (LSK R6) opens the TCAS page.
